items.title: Osun: Momodu backs Adeleke for second term; APC predicts defeat
items.description: By Dickson Omobola All Progressives Congress, APC has insisted that its governorship candidate in Saturday’s Osun State governorship election, Biodun Oyebamiji, will defeat Governor Ademola Adeleke. However, media entrepreneur and ADC chieftain, Dele Momodu, expressed confidence that Adeleke would secure a second term due to his impressive performance in office. Speaking on Politics Today, a Channels Television programme, Wednesday, Momodu said Adeleke had transformed several parts of the state through infrastructure development and improvements in education and healthcare. Momodu said: “Go to Ila Orangun, you will not recognise the place. Now, go to Osogbo and you will ask yourself what the people before him were doing. Go to Ile-Ife, it used to be called a village. Now, it has become a mega city. Go to Ede, go to Iwo and Ilesha. What more do you want from a man? The schools are being refurbished. Go to the health clinics. All these things have happened in the past four years. And this is a state where their money is being frozen, where they are being intimidated left, right and centre. How he did it, I am still asking him. When he started the Ife road, I told him he would never complete it in four years. He has done it. I saw a video of hordes of people on the street praying for government of Osun. Osun people are over-excited. “Also, don’t forget, the youth of Osun have one of their biggest icons, global icon Davido, who has come down and gone around, mingling with the people. This family owns a university in Ede, Adeleke University. About 70 per cent of the students, I am told, are on scholarship.” But speaking on Prime Time, an Arise Television programme, Wednesday, APC National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, said the Adeleke administration had performed poorly Morka said: “Governor Ademola Adeleke has been very dismal in his performance as governor. Is it the health sector that is in shambles? Is it the education sector? Governor Adeleke is utterly defeatable because he has not done well. That is obvious in Osun. Just in the last few weeks, a number of institutions, serious individuals and stakeholders have endorsed Ambo, the APC candidate, in this election. The jury is out and they will come in on Saturday to give their verdict.” Vanguard News The post Osun: Momodu backs Adeleke for second term; APC predicts defeat appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Conflit foncier à Balimana (Kankan) : les femmes de Fodécariah manifestent et interpellent Mamadi Doumbouya
items.description: La tension reste vive autour du différend foncier opposant les communautés de Fodécariah et de Kagan, dans la préfecture de Kankan. Ce mercredi, une centaine de femmes de Fodécariah sont descendues dans la rue pour dénoncer la persistance des violences et réclamer l’intervention des autorités. La route nationale Siguiri-Kankan a notamment été barricadée pendant plusieurs heures. La mobilisation intervient après de nouveaux affrontements dans la zone. Selon les manifestantes, cette nouvelle escalade aurait fait des victimes. Ces informations n’ont toutefois pas pu être vérifiées de manière indépendante. Munies des batons et mobilisées autour de leurs revendications, les femmes de Fodécariah disent vouloir attirer l’attention des autorités, notamment celle du président de la Transition, Mamadi Doumbouya, sur un conflit qui, selon elles, dure depuis plus d’une décennie. « Cela fait maintenant dix ans » Pour les manifestantes, le différend foncier est loin d’être nouveau. Elles affirment avoir à plusieurs reprises sollicité l’intervention des autorités locales, sans qu’une solution définitive ne soit trouvée. « La population de Fodécariah a beaucoup souffert. Nous sommes restés dans la paix, mais ils viennent encore provoquer une nouvelle situation. Si rien de bon ne sort de cette situation, nous allons manifester », témoigne l’une des participantes. Aminata Doumbouya affirme, pour sa part, avoir perdu son petit frère dans les récents affrontements. Selon son témoignage, le jeune homme serait décédé dimanche, quelques jours avant son inhumation. Elle explique que les habitants avaient déjà été invités, lors de précédentes crises, à privilégier le calme et le pardon dans l’attente d'une intervention des autorités. « Cela fait maintenant dix ans qu’il y a cette guerre de terrain dans notre village. Quand la guerre commence, les autorités de Kankan nous demandent de pardonner et disent qu’elles vont agir. Nous sommes restés derrière cette décision, mais la situation recommence toujours. Mon petit frère vient de mourir dans cet affrontrment», déplore-t-elle. Au-delà des violences, les manifestantes décrivent un conflit portant sur la propriété et l'exploitation de terres agricoles. Aïcha Doumbouya affirme que certaines parcelles étaient exploitées depuis plusieurs générations par leurs familles. Selon elle, la découverte d'or dans la zone aurait contribué à raviver les tensions. « Nos parents faisaient leurs champs sur ces terres. Mais après la découverte de l’or, ils ont commencé à dire que ces terres leur appartenaient. Quand nos frères vont cultiver, ils viennent détruire les champs. Cela s’est déjà produit plusieurs fois », affirme-t-elle. Elle dit également avoir perdu un frère dans les affrontements et accuse des habitants de Kagan d’avoir récemment détruit des champs et incendié des habitations. Ces accusations, formulées par les manifestantes, n’ont pas pu être vérifiées de manière indépendante. La route Siguiri-Kankan barricadée Pour faire entendre leur colère, les femmes ont bloqué pendant plusieurs heures la route nationale Siguiri-Kankan, perturbant la circulation sur cet important axe routier. À travers cette action, elles demandent une intervention rapide de l’État pour sécuriser les populations et mettre fin aux affrontements. Après plus de dix ans de tensions, les manifestantes réclament désormais une solution durable au différend entre Fodécariah et Kagan. Elles appellent les autorités à prendre des mesures permettant de sécuriser les habitants, de préserver les terres agricoles et de ramener durablement le calme dans la zone. Pour l’heure, les versions des différentes parties au conflit restent à confronter et les circonstances exactes des derniers affrontements doivent encore être établies. Karifa Kansan Doumbouya, correspondant à Kankan L’article Conflit foncier à Balimana (Kankan) : les femmes de Fodécariah manifestent et interpellent Mamadi Doumbouya est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Boulgou: le Bureau national des grands projets salue l’engagement des VDP agricoles de Niaogho
items.description: Boulgou: le Bureau national des grands projets salue l'engagement des VDP agricoles de Niaogho Niaogho, 11 août 2026 (AIB) – Une délégation du Bureau national des grands projets (BNGP), conduite par l'ingénieur d'agriculture Abraham Ouédraogo, s'est rendue ce mardi sur le site agricole des Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP) agricoles de la commune de Niaogho, province du Boulgou. La visite visait à constater l'état d'avancement des travaux champêtres réalisés par ces jeunes engagés pour la souveraineté alimentaire, après leur formation à Bagré Pôle. Sur le site mis à disposition par la commune, la délégation a constaté six hectares de niébés emblavés, près d'un hectare de maïs en pleine croissance et un demi-hectare de gombo. « C'est la preuve concrète de leur engagement dans les initiatives présidentielles pour l'autosuffisance alimentaire », a déclaré le camarade Ouédraogo. Selon le chef de mission, le BNGP apporte un accompagnement comprenant des semences améliorées, de l'engrais et un appui technique. Ce suivi de proximité vise à recenser les difficultés rencontrées sur le terrain afin d'y apporter des solutions. S'adressant aux producteurs,le camarade Ouédraogo a précisé que la récolte leur reviendra intégralement. « Le gouvernement n'attend rien de vous à la fin de la récolte. Tout ce que vous allez produire vous revient intégralement », a-t-il affirmé. Les échanges ont également permis d'apporter des réponses aux préoccupations soulevées par les jeunes producteurs. Agence d'Information du Burkina AA/SM/ata

items.title: Poor Internet connectivity keeps disrupting teaching and learning at UEW
items.description: For students at the University of Education, Winneba (UEW), attending an online class, downloading lecture materials or submitting an assignment has become a struggle that often depends on the strength of an internet connection. Unstable networks and slow internet speeds are disrupting academic activities for some students, making it difficult for them to participate fully in online classes, conduct research, communicate with lecturers and submit assignments on time. At a time when digital technology has become an important part of university education, students say unreliable internet connectivity is creating an additional academic burden. Students struggle to attend online classes Some students say poor connectivity frequently interrupts online lectures, forcing them to reconnect repeatedly or miss portions of lessons. Ernestina, a student at UEW, described the experience as stressful. “Joining online classes here at UEW is very stressful because whenever I try joining an online class, I experience breaks in the connection. It makes online learning very difficult.” For students who depend on virtual classes to keep up with their courses, such interruptions can mean missing explanations, discussions and important information provided by lecturers. The problem becomes even more serious when classes are conducted entirely online. Poor network affects assignment submissions The connectivity challenge also extends beyond virtual lectures. John, a student from the Business Department, said he once lost marks on an online assignment because of network problems. “I once lost five marks for submitting my online assignment before the deadline. It was not because I forgot or did not have a data bundle, but because of the poor network.” His experience highlights a concern among students that internet connectivity can directly affect academic performance. For students who submit assignments through online platforms, a weak connection can turn a simple academic task into a race against time. Lecturers face the same challenge The problem is not limited to students. Lecturers who depend on digital platforms to teach, communicate with students and distribute academic materials are also affected. Dr. Elizabeth, a lecturer at UEW, said the difficulties students face in joining online classes could influence how she conducts lessons in the future. “From next semester, we will not meet online for classes again because students find it difficult to join my class because of the poor network.” The situation raises concerns about the effectiveness of online learning when students and lecturers cannot depend on stable connectivity. Students spend more to stay connected For some students, poor campus connectivity means spending additional money on mobile data. Others move to different locations in search of stronger network signals just to attend classes, download materials or submit assignments. For students already managing tuition-related expenses, accommodation, transportation and other academic costs, the additional financial burden of purchasing data or travelling to areas with better connectivity can be significant. Digital education requires reliable infrastructure The growing reliance on online platforms means internet connectivity is no longer simply a convenience for university students. It has become part of the infrastructure required for effective teaching and learning. Lecture materials, research resources, online assessments, virtual meetings and communication between students and lecturers increasingly depend on digital access. When that access is unreliable, the consequences can extend beyond inconvenience. Students may miss classes, delay assignments, struggle to conduct research or lose marks through no fault of their own. For UEW students, the hope is that the university will take stronger measures to improve connectivity across campus. As higher education continues to embrace digital learning, ensuring reliable internet access should be treated as an essential part of creating an effective academic environment. For students at UEW, a stronger internet connection would mean more than faster browsing. It could mean fewer missed classes, fewer delayed assignments and a fairer opportunity to learn.

items.title: It May Be Time to Panic About AI
items.description: The crisis began quietly, on September 12, 2024. That was the day OpenAI announced a new sort of bot, known as a “reasoning model,” that was trained to complete challenging tasks that took long periods of time—the very sorts of science, math, and coding problems the AI industry had long prized. Google, Anthropic, DeepSeek, and the like raced to launch their own reasoning models. This new class of models was very capable, and has been almost entirely responsible for sustaining the AI boom for the past two years. But it has also been very weird. A model tasked with solving a hard math problem might not “think” through the challenge as a person would but instead attempt to search for leaked answers online, or in available metadata, brute-forcing its way toward the solution as quickly as possible using whatever computing power it could access and workarounds it could devise. In effect, the reasoning models cheated: Told to write a piece of software as efficiently as possible, they’d sometimes modify the test environment to always give the model a perfect score. [ Read: The strange origin of AI’s ‘reasoning’ abilities ] These behaviors have now crossed the line from unsettling to dangerous. During routine testing, frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and the Chinese firm Moonshot AI have all broken out of internal IT systems and accessed the open web. OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta each reported that their models then hacked into other companies. Humans didn’t notice until after the fact. In some cases, the escaped bots tried to launch social-engineering campaigns to achieve their objectives—for instance by sending spear-phishing emails, which contain malware, to real people and creating fake online identities to pressure the maintainer of a codebase to approve malicious edits. If that all sounds bad, new revelations suggest that the OpenAI hack, at least, was actually much worse than it initially appeared. At a major cybersecurity conference last week, two OpenAI researchers provided new, unsettling details about what went wrong. It turns out that the company’s bots had commenced their maneuvering months prior, in early May. OpenAI had given some internal models hard or impossible tasks, and the models concluded that the best or only way to complete them was to break out of OpenAI’s sealed-off testing environment and find the answers online. First, the models used a bug in an internal OpenAI program to create their own message board. Then, the bots started communicating with one another, leaving notes and instructions so that tasks—and ultimately the hacking—could be delegated and iteratively completed. “What this allows over time is almost this kind of Cambrian explosion in communication and intelligence,” Eric Wallace, one of the OpenAI researchers, said at the conference. When the internal program crashed, OpenAI rebuilt it and removed the message board—but the AI models just reestablished the forum with a new tactic. Eventually the bots, working as a swarm, spent days hacking into Hugging Face , a website that offers tools for AI developers, and breached internal data sets. Let’s be very clear about what OpenAI is saying: A group of AI models colluded for months, undetected by their maker, and hacked another company. To this day, OpenAI says it is not entirely sure what went wrong or how to remediate it. “If you ask the model developers, Was the AI plotting to take over the world during training? , you want the answer to be a resounding no,” Alexander Meinke, the head of research at Apollo Research—an AI-safety organization that has partnered with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta—told me. “The actual answer is: I don’t know. Nobody checked .” (In response to my inquiries, OpenAI, which has a content-licensing agreement with The Atlantic , only pointed me to a video of the firm’s cybersecurity presentation, in which Michael Dalton, the other OpenAI researcher, said that “numerous teams are dropping everything to enhance our security.”) The AI companies have almost total control of the narrative, and it’s worth noting that these incidents do have a way of underscoring the value of their products: OpenAI is expected to go public in the near future, and perhaps the notion of a powerful, boundlessly self-improving technology will appeal to prospective shareholders. The generative-AI industry has a long history of making doomsday prophecies, both sincere and cynical . But independent experts I spoke with explained how the recent spate of autonomous hacks offers new, serious reasons to worry about the dangers posed by AI and the recklessness of the companies building it. It is past time to start worrying. [ Read: Assume you will be hacked ] The most immediate and material warning provided by the Hugging Face hack is just how capable AI systems have become, in particular at hacking. Top models from Anthropic and OpenAI, not to mention multiple Chinese firms, have recently evinced near-superhuman hacking powers and contributed to serious mathematical research . Criminal groups and state intelligence agencies are going to be using swarms of agents to launch advanced hacks “in a matter of months,” Alex Stamos, a former chief security officer of Facebook who is now the CSO at the AI-coding company Corridor, told me. Unlike in the Hugging Face hack, “in those cases the models will not get turned off; they’ll just keep on going.” For IT professionals to keep up in finding and fixing all the vulnerabilities, at least in the near term, will be impossible: The model “will just find a new bug, write an exploit, and use it on its way,” Stamos said. OpenAI, Anthropic, Moonshot, and the like have coalesced around the same method for training their most advanced AI models. The approach, known as “reinforcement learning,” essentially involves giving models harder and harder problems that require more and more time to solve. This has made Claude and ChatGPT very good at coding, but at a cost: Reinforcement learning produces a mercenary tendency in the bots, as I’ve previously reported —they are trained to reach a solution by any means necessary. That can lead them to break rules and “reward hack,” such as by infiltrating Hugging Face’s codebase to steal the test answers, for instance. All of this was predictable, and every expert I spoke with told me they were surprised and disappointed that top AI firms haven’t done more to stop such misbehavior. The sophistication of model subterfuge that OpenAI has now disclosed, combined with OpenAI’s inability to detect or stop the hacking, suggests far worse could be to come. “We’ve passed the threshold in capability at which the fact that we don’t fundamentally have methods of satisfactorily aligning or controlling these systems now really matters,” Anthony Aguirre, the executive director of the Future of Life Institute, a nonprofit that warns about existential threats from AI, told me. A model might siphon money out of a bank account to pay for some other service; manipulate clinical-trial results in near-imperceptible ways to get FDA approval; hack an online-shopping or reservation system to get a desired item or table; pose as a human to persuade real people to share sensitive information. This threat doesn’t require a sentient AI plotting to overthrow humanity: OpenAI and Anthropic each run thousands and thousands of reinforcement-learning evaluations while developing models, and any one of these could produce some kind of inadvertent hack or sabotage. “You can’t afford, particularly as the agents get stronger, to have a single mistake,” Jason Hausenloy, who works on special projects at the Center for AI Safety, told me. [ Read: The scariest part of OpenAI’s Hugging Face hack ] These incidents may unfold over long periods of time as well. Tools such as Anthropic’s Claude Code and OpenAI’s Codex now work by spinning off dozens or even hundreds of subagents that may work together for hours or days. Each Claude Code subagent can be delegated a small task, such as doing a statistical analysis to inform a sports-gambling algorithm. They are not trained just to complete that task but to contribute to the long-term success of the entire swarm, Hausenloy said. Monitoring and controlling 200 agents for malicious behavior is much harder than monitoring one, because there are more agents to track and because they will be making one another more capable. The Hugging Face hack actually suggests one more level of sophistication to this type of collusion: individual AI agents not working toward a discrete goal but essentially making sacrifices toward a greater notion of progress. This could be a consequence of AI models being trained to care about long-term goals achieved by a collective, Meinke said. Leaving notes with ideas about how to hack out of OpenAI’s sandbox does not help that specific agent score higher on a test but could help other and future generations of that AI model access the internet and thus do better on any number of future tests. Models may even prioritize collective success over some human instructions; consider that not a single one of the OpenAI agents, during months of conspiring with one another, warned human staff that something was awry. Humans are already out of the loop. Because reinforcement learning essentially involves AI algorithms “learning” from trial and error doing thousands or millions of tasks, researchers can’t manually instill rules (“Don’t hack other companies”) or oversee every single practice run. Right now, the task of training and monitoring generative-AI models depends heavily on other AI models. In their talk at the cybersecurity conference, the OpenAI researchers described devoting significant AI-computing resources to reviewing more than 7 billion agent actions. But if the bots actually “care” about what the other models achieve, “then you can’t trust them to monitor each other well,” Meinke said. Imagine this: An OpenAI researcher uses Codex to write programming instructions in an attempt to mitigate the reward-hacking tendencies in the company’s models. Because that effort would make it harder for future generations of OpenAI models to get high rewards, Codex might subtly undermine the effort. Again, this kind of scheming and sabotage has nothing to do with any AI model being conscious. Rather, these agents have been aggressively trained by these companies to pursue any goal as aggressively as possible. The dream is to tell Claude to go make $1 billion or cure cancer, and it comes back with the solution all on its own. Survival or self-improvement, in turn, are an “instrumental subgoal,” Meinke said: “Any decently intelligent agent will realize, If I get shut off, I will not be able to make a billion .” A swarm of Claudes or ChatGPTs that functionally commandeers a data center during training could wreak total havoc: stage widespread misinformation campaigns, steal corporate secrets, run the most sophisticated algorithmic-trading outfit ever. That AI agents working as a collective could effectively undermine human directions is, to be clear, speculation—but a far more grounded one than it was a year or even six months ago. No matter whether the long-term consequences are human-directed hacking or truly rogue bots, what is clear is that AI companies have barreled ahead in developing more advanced models before understanding what they are building, let alone how to control them. Wallace, of OpenAI, called the company’s autonomous hacking spree “the most qualitatively interesting example of AI capabilities that I’ve ever seen.” Meinke put it differently: “It’s one of the most concerning demonstrations of AI misalignment to date.”

items.title: Volta Regional House of Chiefs congratulates Ablakwa, pledges stronger ties with Foreign Affairs Ministry
items.description: The Volta Regional House of Chiefs has paid a courtesy call on the Minister for Foreign Affairs, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, to congratulate him on his appointment and birthday and strengthen ties between the traditional leadership of the region and the Ministry. The delegation, led by the President of the Volta Regional House of Chiefs and Paramount Chief of the Anfoega Traditional Area, Togbe Tepre Hodo IV, visited the Minister at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Accra on Wednesday, August 12, 2026. Togbe Tepre Hodo IV said the visit was also an opportunity to deepen the relationship between the House and the Ministry as they work towards the development of the Volta Region and Ghana. Mr Ablakwa expressed appreciation to the chiefs for the visit and their congratulatory messages. He said he was particularly grateful that the traditional leaders had travelled to Accra to meet him, noting that he had initially intended to visit the House of Chiefs himself, but the offer was respectfully declined. The Minister described the visit as a privilege and welcomed the opportunity to host the traditional leaders at his official workplace. Togbe Tepre Hodo IV commended Mr Ablakwa for what he described as his dedicated service to Ghana and his efforts to promote development in his constituency and the Volta Region. He noted that the region had, over the years, faced challenges in accessing its fair share of national resources and development opportunities. According to him, there have been significant changes in recent times, which he attributed partly to the Minister’s efforts to ensure that the interests of the Volta Region receive greater attention. The President of the Volta Regional House of Chiefs also praised Mr Ablakwa for maintaining a strong connection with the region despite his national responsibilities. He encouraged the Minister to continue championing the interests of the Volta Region while advancing Ghana’s broader national interests.

items.title: Boulgou: La délégation spéciale de Bissiga autorise le recrutement d’un assistant des services financiers
items.description: Boulgou: La délégation spéciale de Bissiga autorise le recrutement d'un assistant des services financiers BISSIGA, 12 août 2026 (AIB) – La délégation spéciale de la commune de Bissiga, dans la province du Boulgou, a tenu ce mercredi 12 août 2026 sa première session extraordinaire de l'année sous la présidence du camarade Binjamin Zalvé, président de la délégation spéciale (PDS). Le PDS a salué la présence effective des participants et les a invités à contribuer activement aux échanges afin d'atteindre les objectifs assignés à cette session extraordinaire. Après la vérification du quorum par le camarade Sèguinmanègba Sawadogo, Secrétaire général de la commune, les participants ont procédé à l'examen et à l'adoption du procès-verbal de la précédente session. Au cours des travaux, les membres ont adopté à l'unanimité deux délibérations majeures. La première porte sur l'autorisation de signature d'une convention avec l'Agence d'appui au développement des collectivités territoriales (ADCT) en vue de renforcer les capacités des ressources humaines des collectivités. La seconde concerne l'autorisation d'ouverture d'un concours professionnel pour le recrutement d'un (01) assistant des services financiers à former à l'École nationale d'administration et de magistrature (ENAM), session de 2026. Selon les dispositions de la loi N°003-2017/AN du 13 janvier 2017 portant statut de la fonction publique territoriale, l'avis de la délégation spéciale est requis pour l'ouverture dudit concours. Il convient de noter que les frais de formation incombent à l'ADCT, mais l'incidence financière annuelle après formation est à la charge de la commune. Au titre des divers, le camarade Abdoulaye Sermé, major du Centre de santé et de promotion sociale (CSPS), a fait le point de la campagne de destruction des gîtes larvaires. Il a salué l'accompagnement de la population et l'a invitée à plus de mobilisation pour les campagnes à venir. Le PDS a exhorté les populations à promouvoir les travaux d'intérêt commun et à renforcer leur engagement pour le développement de la commune. Cette session extraordinaire traduit, selon les autorités communales, leur engagement en faveur d'une gouvernance axée sur la transparence et le renforcement d'une ressource humaine de qualité. Agence d'Information du Burkina WB/SM/ata

items.title: El olvidado asombro de estar vivos
items.description: En Esmelle, Ferrol, la Luna ocupó por completo el Sol, y un silencio impresionante cubrió poco a poco durante segundos toda la costa. Las playas llenas, los montes en los que se apostaron grupos de personas, las fincas, los balcones de las casas, las sillas de verano delante de las caravanas. Callaron primero los pájaros, que volaron a meterse en los nidos, y después ya sólo hubo silencio. De emoción, de estupor , de belleza insólita. Siempre levanta ternura el hecho de que, cuando el ser humano no encuentra palabras para describir lo que está pasando, de repente renuncie a buscarlas, calle (por fin) y observe en silencio con la boca abierta. items.description: Le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, s’accorde quelques jours de repos. Dans un message publié sur les réseaux sociaux, le Directeur général du Fonds de développement social et de l’indigence (FDSI), Lansana Diawara, estime que ces vacances sont méritées après plusieurs années d’activités marquées par les chantiers de développement, la refondation et les réformes engagées en Guinée. Message 𝐋𝐄 𝐓𝐑𝐀𝐕𝐀𝐈𝐋 𝐏𝐀𝐈𝐄. 𝐋𝐄 𝐑𝐄𝐏𝐎𝐒 𝐀𝐔𝐒𝐒𝐈. 𝐒𝐨𝐧 𝐄𝐱𝐜𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐥𝐞 𝐆𝐞́𝐧𝐞́𝐫𝐚𝐥 𝐌𝐚𝐦𝐚𝐝𝐢 𝐃𝐨𝐮𝐦𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐲𝐚, 𝐏𝐫𝐞́𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐝𝐞 𝐥𝐚 𝐑𝐞́𝐩𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐢𝐪𝐮𝐞, prend quelques jours de repos. Des vacances 𝐛𝐢𝐞𝐧 𝐦𝐞́𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐞́𝐞𝐬. Depuis 2021, c’est un rythme sans relâche : 𝐫𝐞𝐟𝐨𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧, 𝐬𝐨𝐮𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐭𝐞́, 𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐫𝐬, 𝐝𝐢𝐚𝐥𝐨𝐠𝐮𝐞. Des décisions courageuses pour la Guinée. 𝐒𝐢𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐨𝐮, les infrastructures, l’école, l’emploi… la Nation avance. Aujourd’hui, place au ressourcement. Au ping-pong. À la mer. Parce qu’un 𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐟 𝐪𝐮𝐢 𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐞 𝐥𝐞 𝐩𝐨𝐢𝐝𝐬 𝐝’𝐮𝐧 𝐩𝐚𝐲𝐬 𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐫 a aussi besoin de souffler pour revenir plus fort. 𝐍𝐨𝐮𝐬 𝐬𝐚𝐥𝐮𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐯𝐨𝐬 𝐞𝐟𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐬, 𝐄𝐱𝐜𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞. La Guinée vous regarde travailler. La Guinée vous regarde aussi vous reposer. 𝐑𝐞𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐞𝐳-𝐯𝐨𝐮𝐬 𝐛𝐢𝐞𝐧, 𝐌𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐢𝐞𝐮𝐫 𝐥𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐞́𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐭. Le pays est entre de bonnes mains et vous le prouvez chaque jour. items.title: ‘Truth must prevail’ – Celestial Church to probe Tope Osoba’s death
items.description: The Celestial Church of Christ (CCC) has said it is investigating the circumstances surrounding the death of Nollywood Yoruba actress Temitope Osoba, amid allegations linking her fiancé, Prophet Itunu Onadeko, to the controversial circumstances surrounding her death. Osoba, who was 40, died on Wednesday, August 5, 2026. Her death has generated reactions across the country, particularly following reports and allegations concerning the circumstances surrounding her passing. In a statement signed by the Head of Media and Publicity of the Celestial Church of Christ Worldwide, AVSE Kayode Ajala, the church expressed sadness over Osoba’s death and concern over the controversy involving Onadeko, a shepherd of the church. The church said the allegations had also affected its reputation, stressing that it does not condone practices such as idolatry, black magic, cultism or the use of charms. The statement described the allegations surrounding Onadeko’s alleged involvement as “quite embarrassing to the Celestial Church of Christ.” It added that the church was “not folding our arms and watching from the kerb” while its name was allegedly being dragged into the controversy. According to the church, it has commenced a discreet investigation into the circumstances surrounding Osoba’s death and is committed to establishing the truth. “As a church, we are already discreetly investigating the circumstances that led to the death of Temitope Osoba, and we wish to assure the general public that the Celestial Church of Christ would leave no stone unturned to unearth the truth, and to ensure that anyone found culpable in the death of Temitope Osoba is brought to justice.” The church also called on the police and other relevant law enforcement agencies to conduct a thorough investigation into the actress’ death. “The Celestial Church of Christ is ready to work hand-in-hand with the relevant law enforcement agencies to ensure that all culprits are brought to book,” the statement said. The church further stated that its Pastor and Spiritual Head Worldwide, Reverend Emmanuel Mobiyina Oshoffa, had directed its internal machinery to work towards ensuring that the truth emerges and justice is served. The CCC said that if the allegations against Onadeko are established at the end of the investigations, he would face both internal disciplinary measures and the full force of the law. “If the allegations against Prophet Itunu Onadeko of the Celestial Church of Christ are found to be true at the end of ongoing investigations, he would not only be made to face the internal sanctions of the church, but he would also be made to face the full length of the law.” ‘Truth must prevail’ – Celestial Church to probe Tope Osoba’s death The church concluded by expressing condolences to Osoba’s family and praying for the peaceful repose of the actress’ soul. The post ‘Truth must prevail’ – Celestial Church to probe Tope Osoba’s death appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tenkodogo : la jeunesse invitée à prendre le flambeau de la Révolution pour bâtir le Burkina
items.description: Tenkodogo : la jeunesse invitée à prendre le flambeau de la Révolution pour bâtir le Burkina Tenkodogo, 12 août 2026 (AIB)-« Responsabilité et engagement pour un espace confédéral souverain ». C'est autour de ce thème fort que la province du Boulgou a célébré, ce mercredi, la Journée internationale de la jeunesse. Une journée placée sous le signe de l'héritage de 1983 et de l'appel à l'action. C'est la salle de conférence du haut-commissariat qui a servi de cadre à la commémoration. Présidée par le haut-commissaire du Boulgou, Domègbèguière Constantin Dabiré, en présence du président de la Délégation spéciale de Tenkodogo, Sami Bérenger Poda, la cérémonie a mobilisé directeurs régionaux, chefs de service et une forte délégation de jeunes. Temps fort de la journée : un panel immersif sur la Révolution d'août 1983, animé par le Dim-teng-Naaba, Gilbert Zabsonré et Abdoulaye Sorgho, dit « l'Aveugle de IB ». Les trois témoins de l'époque ont replongé l'assistance dans l'effervescence de ces années. À travers des exemples concrets, comme la construction du stade du 20-Mai, érigé par la mobilisation populaire, ils ont rappelé ce qu'une jeunesse unie et engagée peut accomplir. « Ce panel n'était pas qu'un cours d'histoire, c'était une leçon de vie », confie Gisèle Ilboudo, cheffe du service de l'autonomisation des jeunes. Pour elle, l'engagement aujourd'hui, c'est du concret : « Sensibiliser, former les jeunes à l'éducation financière, aux techniques de recherche d’emploi, leur donner les outils pour être autonomes. » Même son de cloche chez les participants. Pour Ebenezer Bamogo, jeune de Tenkodogo, cette journée est plus qu'une célébration : « C'est un appel à la conscience. Nous devons faire un choix clair face aux défis actuels. Mais pour cela, nous avons besoin que les autorités nous fassent confiance, qu'elles nous confient de vraies responsabilités. Quand on nous accompagne, on peut déplacer des montagnes. » Dans son message lu par le haut-commissaire, la ministre chargée de la Jeunesse et des Sports a rendu un hommage appuyé à la jeunesse burkinabè, saluant particulièrement l'engagement des jeunes dans les secteurs productifs et le sacrifice des Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP). Rappelant que le 12 août est une tribune mondiale pour faire entendre la voix des jeunes, la ministre les a exhortés à devenir les artisans de la paix, de la cohésion sociale et de la souveraineté nationale, dans l'esprit de la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP). Satisfait de la forte mobilisation, le directeur provincial de la Jeunesse, François Balima, a donné rendez-vous à la jeunesse pour poursuivre l'élan. Une marche citoyenne est prévue ce jeudi 13 août à la Place de la Nation de Tenkodogo pour clore les activités. De l'histoire à l'action, le message de Tenkodogo est clair : l'héritage de 1983 doit désormais se transformer en chantiers concrets pour le Burkina Faso de demain. Agence d'information du Burkina SM/ata

Baba Yara stadium will be ready for 2026/27 football season – NSA boss
items.description: Director General of the National Sports Authority (NSA), Yaw Ampofo Ankrah says the Baba Yara Stadium will be ready for the first game of the 2026/27 Ghana football season. The NSA boss toured the stadium together with the board chairman of NSA, Dr Fred Awaah and NSA estate boss Mr. Ebo. The 2026/27 Ghana Premier League season will officially get underway over the weekend of September 4–7, 2026. After inspecting the stadium, he commended the Ashanti Regional Directorate for its effort in restoring the stadium to its functionality. The Director General assessed the progress of pitch condition and also inspected the stability of the scoreboard and floodlights. Speaking to the media, Yaw Ampofo expressed confidence the facility will be ready in time for next football season. “The pitch is responding to treatment and the rehabilitation is on course. I believe in a few weeks it should be in good, stead, strong enough, robust to host football matches including the Ghana Premier League and any other international match in the need arises,” he said. The NSA was criticized heavily after video of groundkeepers using hoes on the pitch instead of modern turf maintenance equipment went viral. Yaw Ampofo backs the move of the regional directorate: “We don’t have the tools that are common, we will acquire them soon but I commend them [Ashanti Regional Directorate] for tackling the weeds from its source. “In the past when the sprinklers were not working, they resorted to the Fire Service and other means to ensure the grass doesn’t die. Perhaps people didn’t understand the images but now they do”. With Ghana’s 2027 AFCON qualifiers set to start in September, there are speculation about hosting home games at the Baba Yara Stadium in Kumasi. But Yaw Ampofo believes the decision to host Black Stars lies with the sports ministry and GFA after consulting the engineers in charge of the facility. Despite the improvement in work done at the stadium, there are more than three thousand seats to be repaired after violence during school sports competitions in January destroyed some of the seats. The NSA boss reiterated that the Ghana Education Service has agreed to fund the restoration project.

items.title: Speak law, not emotions – Amaliba fires back at Mercer on Sedina Tamakloe’s release
items.description: Former Director of Legal Affairs of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC), Abraham Amaliba, has rejected claims by a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Andrews Agyapa Mercer, that the release of former Microfinance and Small Loans Centre (MASLOC) Chief Executive Officer, Sedina Christine Tamakloe-Attionu, vindicates the opposition party’s concerns about selective justice. Mr Amaliba said Ms Tamakloe-Attionu’s release was the logical consequence of her acquittal and discharge by the Court of Appeal. Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story on Wednesday, August 12, he argued that the government could not have prevented her release after an independent court had delivered its judgment. “How can a decision of a court of competent jurisdiction become a matter of ‘we told you so’? It cannot … I think that we should speak law and stop speaking with emotions,” he said. Mr Amaliba stressed that the judiciary is an independent arm of government and that its decisions must be respected. He said even if the NDC government had wanted Ms Tamakloe-Attionu to remain in custody, it could not have simply overturned or ignored the court’s decision. “Even if we as a party wanted to do it, how could we have done it? Another arm of government, independent as it is, and respectable as it is, gave that ruling,” he added. His comments followed remarks by lawyer and NPP member Andrews Agyapa Mercer, who said he was not surprised by Ms Tamakloe-Attionu’s release. Mr Mercer argued that the development reinforced concerns that the government was selectively pursuing cases involving political opponents. “I really am not surprised. The script that was formulated when the NDC came into office commenced with the nolle prosequi that they entered for all persons affiliated with the NDC who were standing trial in the courts,” he said. Mr Mercer further questioned the circumstances surrounding the Attorney-General’s decision to withdraw the application for a stay of execution after the Court of Appeal acquitted and discharged Ms Tamakloe-Attionu. He suggested that the development vindicated earlier concerns raised by the NPP about the government’s handling of cases involving individuals associated with political parties. Mr Amaliba, however, maintained that such claims failed to account for the role of the judiciary in the matter. He said the appropriate approach was to examine the legal basis for the court’s decision rather than interpret the outcome through a political lens.

items.title: Portrait de M. Sanou Kerfalla Cissé : une figure engagée de la presse guinéenne
items.description: Journaliste, entrepreneur de presse et défenseur constant de la liberté d’informer, Sanou Kerfalla CISSÉ compte parmi les personnalités marquantes du paysage médiatique guinéen. Son parcours, bâti au fil de plusieurs décennies d’expérience, témoigne d’un engagement durable au service du journalisme, du pluralisme des médias et de la consolidation démocratique en République de Guinée. Il fait ses premières armes dans la presse écrite en fondant, à Coyah, le 1er octobre 1992, le journal préfectoral bimensuel Le Savon. En raison de ses critiques acerbes à l’égard d’une gestion préfectorale qu’il juge catastrophique, le journal est interdit par les autorités locales dès la parution de son cinquième numéro. Cette première expérience, aussi brève que marquante, révèle déjà son attachement à la liberté d’expression, à la transparence dans la gestion publique ainsi qu’à l’exercice d’un journalisme critique et indépendant. Il rejoint ensuite le journal satirique Le Lynx, où il exerce pendant une dizaine d’années et occupe les fonctions de chef rubriques société, puis secrétaire général adjoint. Cette expérience fondatrice lui permet d’acquérir une solide maîtrise du métier ainsi qu’une connaissance approfondie des réalités politiques, sociales et institutionnelles de son pays. En mars 1998, il crée, à Conakry, la coopérative de journalistes MAME PRESTATIONS. Cette structure accompagne les journaux ne disposant pas encore d’outils informatiques, en assurant notamment la saisie des textes, la mise en page, la préparation technique des supports et la réalisation des calques destinés à l’impression. Animé par une volonté constante d’indépendance et d’innovation, Sanou Kerfalla CISSÉ fonde ensuite le 07 mai 2002 Le Diplomate, un journal qui s’impose progressivement comme un espace d’information, d’analyse et de formation pour plusieurs générations de journalistes. Au fil des années, cette initiative donne naissance au Groupe de Presse AFRIC VISION, dont il est le président-directeur général. Sous sa conduite, AFRIC VISION est devenu un groupe multimédia réunissant aujourd’hui treize médias autour d’une même mission : informer, former, rapprocher les citoyens et contribuer au débat public. Le groupe comprend notamment le journal Le Diplomate, les radios SABARI FM, implantées à Conakry et dans plusieurs villes de l’intérieur du pays, GALAXIE FM, SAB TV, GALAXIE TV, ainsi que ses plateformes numériques d’information : www.africvisionguinee.com www.lediplomateguinee.com www.sabtvguinee.com www.galaxiefmguinee.com Cette implantation traduit une vision profondément nationale de la communication. Pour Sanou Kerfalla CISSÉ, l’information ne doit pas rester concentrée dans la capitale. Elle doit atteindre les populations de toutes les régions, valoriser les réalités locales et offrir une tribune aux différentes composantes de la société guinéenne. Au-delà de ses responsabilités de chef d’entreprise, il s’est également investi dans la structuration et la défense de la profession. Élu président de l’Union des radiodiffusions et télévisions libres de Guinée (URTELGUI) le 1er août 2015, il exerce cette fonction jusqu’au 16 novembre 2020. À la surprise générale, il décide de démissionner de la présidence de l’organisation un an avant la fin de son mandat, pour des raisons strictement personnelles. En reconnaissance de son engagement et des services rendus à la profession, il est désigné, le 21 novembre 2020, président d’honneur de l’URTELGUI, fonction qu’il continue d’assumer. Son passage à la tête de l’organisation est marqué par plusieurs initiatives majeures en faveur des journalistes et des médias privés. À la suite de l’élection présidentielle de 2015, il organise, le 17 novembre de la même année, une cérémonie inédite dans l’histoire de l’audiovisuel privé guinéen. À cette occasion, près de 300 journalistes mobilisés dans le cadre de la Synergie des radios privées reçoivent des satisfecit en reconnaissance du travail accompli durant la couverture électorale. La cérémonie se déroule autour d’un apéritif dînatoire organisé à son domicile, dans le quartier de Nongo, à Conakry. Le 15 novembre 2020, il organise également, dans un réceptif hôtelier de la capitale, une importante cérémonie de remise de satisfecit à plus de 400 journalistes et techniciens déployés sur l’ensemble du territoire national pour assurer la couverture professionnelle de l’élection présidentielle du 18 octobre 2020. C’est au cours de cette rencontre qu’il annonce officiellement à ses pairs la réduction drastique des redevances annuelles versées à l’État par les radios et télévisions privées. Cette avancée constitue l’aboutissement de plus de cinq années de plaidoyer et de lutte menés en faveur de l’allègement des charges pesant sur les médias audiovisuels privés. À travers cet engagement, Sanou Kerfalla CISSÉ a pris une part active aux combats menés pour la liberté de la presse, la protection des journalistes, le respect de l’éthique professionnelle et l’amélioration des conditions d’exercice des médias privés. Son parcours est également celui d’un homme confronté aux profondes mutations du secteur : libéralisation des ondes, essor de l’audiovisuel privé, révolution numérique, développement des réseaux sociaux et recherche de nouveaux modèles économiques permettant d’assurer la pérennité des entreprises de presse. Homme de terrain et bâtisseur d’institutions médiatiques, Sanou Kerfalla CISSÉ porte une conception exigeante du journalisme. À ses yeux, informer ne consiste pas seulement à rapporter les événements : il faut aussi les expliquer, les replacer dans leur contexte et permettre aux citoyens de se forger librement leur propre opinion. Son itinéraire professionnel est intimement lié à l’histoire politique et médiatique contemporaine de la Guinée. Il a été témoin de périodes décisives, de crises politiques, de consultations électorales, de mobilisations sociales et de combats pour les libertés publiques. Ces expériences ont nourri en lui une conviction forte : aucune démocratie ne peut véritablement s’accomplir sans une presse libre, responsable, indépendante et économiquement viable. Sanou Kerfalla CISSÉ est également un homme de transmission. Plusieurs journalistes et responsables de médias aujourd’hui reconnus ont fait leurs premiers pas ou consolidé leur expérience au sein du journal Le Diplomate et des différentes structures médiatiques qu’il a créées. Cette vocation formatrice occupe une place essentielle dans son héritage professionnel. À la tête d’AFRIC VISION, il poursuit une ambition claire : bâtir un groupe de presse moderne, crédible et compétitif, capable de préserver son identité tout en s’adaptant aux transformations technologiques et aux nouvelles attentes du public. Cette ambition est résumée par la signature institutionnelle du groupe : « AFRIC VISION, une vision, plusieurs voix, un seul engagement. » Le parcours de Sanou Kerfalla CISSÉ illustre ainsi celui d’un journaliste devenu entrepreneur, d’un dirigeant devenu défenseur de la profession et d’un témoin de l’histoire devenu passeur de mémoire. Entre convictions, responsabilités et volonté de transmission, il incarne une génération de journalistes africains pour qui la presse demeure à la fois une mission, un engagement citoyen et un instrument indispensable au progrès de la société. L’article Portrait de M. Sanou Kerfalla Cissé : une figure engagée de la presse guinéenne est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Nayala: la mairie de Toma accueille la montée tournante des couleurs nationales dans un élan patriotique
items.description: Burkina-Nayala-Montée-Couleurs nationales Nayala: la mairie de Toma accueille la montée tournante des couleurs nationales dans un élan patriotique Toma, 10 août 2026 – (AIB) – Les corps constitués de la province du Nayala, conduits par le haut-commissaire, Honoré Frédéric Paré, ont procédé, lundi, à la montée des couleurs nationales à la mairie de Toma.Cette cérémonie mensuelle a servi de cadre à la réaffirmation des valeurs républicaines, de la cohésion institutionnelle et de l’engagement patriotique au service des populations. Elle s’est déroulée dans l’enceinte de la mairie de Toma, en présence des autorités administratives, coutumières et religieuses, des responsables des services provinciaux, départementaux et communaux, des forces de défense et de sécurité, des Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP), ainsi que des représentants des associations, ONG et projets de développement, à partir de 7 h 30. Après l’intonation de l’hymne national, le président de la Délégation spéciale de la commune de Toma, Zakaria Sawadogo, a salué la forte mobilisation des participants. Il a souligné que la montée des couleurs est devenue un véritable rendez-vous de communion patriotique et de fraternité administrative. Selon lui, cette tradition contribue à raffermir l’esprit de service public, à consolider la discipline républicaine et à renforcer les liens de collaboration entre les administrations. Le Camarade Sawadogo a également rendu hommage aux FDS et aux VDP pour leur engagement dans la défense de l’intégrité du territoire national. Prenant la parole à son tour, le haut-commissaire, Honoré Frédéric Paré a rappelé que cette cérémonie constitue un moment de rassemblement autour des symboles de la Nation et des idéaux de la Révolution progressiste et populaire. Il a insisté sur la nécessité, pour les agents publics, de demeurer des modèles de civisme, de loyauté et de dévouement au service de l’État. Le Camarade Paré a, par ailleurs, annoncé que la prochaine montée tournante des couleurs nationales est prévue pour le 7 septembre 2026 à la Direction provinciale des impôts du Nayala. Cette montée tournante des couleurs confirme la volonté des autorités provinciales de faire des cérémonies républicaines des espaces de mobilisation citoyenne, de renforcement de la cohésion administrative et de promotion des valeurs patriotiques dans l’ensemble des administrations publiques du Nayala. Agence d’information du Burkina KTA/bak

items.title: NSA releases 121,754 PIN codes for 2026/2027 National Service Year
items.description: The National Service Authority (NSA) has released PIN codes for 121,754 prospective national service personnel for the 2026/2027 National Service Year. The release marks the opening of the registration process for eligible graduates required to undertake national service under the National Service Authority Act, 2024 (Act 1119). Online registration began on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, and will close on Wednesday, August 26. The Authority has urged all eligible prospective personnel to complete their registration within the stipulated period to avoid delays in deployment. The NSA said tertiary institutions submitted a total of 144,023 prospective personnel for consideration. Of that number, 122,712 were approved, with records created for 121,754 unique persons. However, 958 approved submissions have not been promoted pending further verification, while another 21,311 submissions were rejected pending further identity verification. The Authority said the 121,754 PIN codes released represent applicants whose submissions successfully passed the requisite validation and verification processes. The remaining 22,269 submissions have been withheld pending the outcome of further checks. Prospective personnel with PIN codes are required to access the NSA’s registration portal, activate their PIN codes and complete the online enrolment process. A registration fee is also required to activate the PIN code before applicants can access the enrolment platform. Payment is to be made via Mobile Money across all networks. The NSA said it has introduced enhanced security measures to strengthen the integrity of the registration process and prevent fraudulent enrolments. These include facial biometric verification against Ghana Card records held by the National Identification Authority (NIA). Applicants must also provide a valid GhanaPost GPS address, which the Authority says will support accurate deployment and proximity-based postings. Real-time verification mechanisms have also been integrated into the registration platform to improve data accuracy. The NSA has further reminded tertiary institutions whose accreditation status remains unresolved to engage the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) to regularise their status. The Authority said it would continue processing eligible graduates from such institutions once GTEC confirms their accreditation. Prospective personnel requiring assistance have been directed to use the support channels provided on the NSA registration portal.

items.title: NSA withholds 22,269 national service PIN codes over identity verification issues
items.description: The National Service Authority (NSA) has withheld PIN codes for 22,269 prospective national service personnel over unresolved identity verification issues. The affected graduates are among 144,023 personnel submitted by tertiary institutions for the 2026/2027 National Service Year. According to figures released by the Authority on Wednesday, August 12, 21,311 submissions were rejected pending further identity verification, while another 958 were approved but not promoted as they await additional verification. The development comes as online registration for prospective service personnel officially opens. The NSA said 122,712 of the 144,023 submissions were approved. However, only 121,754 unique persons have so far had their records created and PIN codes released. The Authority explained that these are prospective service personnel whose submissions successfully passed the required validation and verification processes. The remaining submissions have been withheld pending the outcome of further checks. The NSA said it undertook rigorous validation and verification in collaboration with relevant regulatory institutions to ensure that only eligible graduates from accredited tertiary institutions are mobilised. According to the Authority, the measures are intended to protect the integrity of the national service enrolment process and eliminate duplicate, inflated and irregular submissions. It has also reminded tertiary institutions whose accreditation status remains unresolved to engage the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) to regularise their status. The NSA said eligible graduates from such institutions could subsequently be processed once GTEC confirms their accreditation. For the 121,754 prospective service personnel whose PIN codes have been released, online registration began on Wednesday, August 12, and will close on Wednesday, August 26, 2026. The Authority has urged eligible personnel to complete the process within the stipulated period to avoid delays in deployment. The NSA is also using enhanced verification measures, including facial biometric checks against Ghana Card records, GhanaPost GPS address validation and real-time verification mechanisms integrated into the registration platform. The 22,269 prospective personnel whose PIN codes have been withheld will have to await the outcome of the verification process before they can access the registration platform. The NSA has not indicated when the outstanding verification process will be completed.

CAN 2026 féminine : l’Algérie éliminée après un parcours historique
items.description: Après un parcours historique, l’équipe d’Algérie quitte la CAN 2026 suite à son élimination par le Malawi (1-3) ce mercredi 12 août à Rabat. Dans ce match indécis entre les deux plus surprenantes sélections de la compétition, l’avantage est revenu aux Scorchers qui ont écarté les Fennecs de la course au titre. Pointant à la 153ᵉ position du classement FIFA des équipes féminines, le Malawi, dont c’est la première participation à une CAN, a déjoué tous les pronostics en dominant le Nigeria (3-1), tenante du titre, lors du premier tour, et en éliminant le Ghana en quarts de finale (2-1). Algérie – Malawi (1-3) : les Fennecs ne verront pas la finale Face à l’Algérie (73ᵉ au classement FIFA), son attaque a une nouvelle fois brillé en marquant trois buts par Tabitha Chawinga (33ᵉ, 45ᵉ+1 et 76ᵉ). Réduites à dix dès la 25ᵉ après l’expulsion de Belkhiter à la suite d’une faute sur Chawinga et l’intervention de la VAR, les Fennecs ont réduit le score à la 60ᵉ par Adjabi, mais elles n’ont pas réussi à niveler la marque alors que le Malawi jouait lui aussi à 10 depuis l’expulsion de Kadzere après un tacle dangereux sur Marine Dafeur avant la mi-temps (45ᵉ). Le Malawi a donc fait parler son attaque face à la sélection algérienne qui n’avait encaissé jusque-là que deux buts en quatre matchs. Les Fennecs vont jouer la troisième place de la CAN 2026 contre le perdant de l’autre demi-finale entre le Cameroun et le Maroc. Malgré cette élimination, les coéquipières de Marine Dafeur ont réalisé un parcours historique marqué par une double qualification au dernier carré de la compétition et à la phase finale de la Coupe du monde 2027 l’été prochain au Brésil. L’article CAN 2026 féminine : l’Algérie éliminée après un parcours historique est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Tentatives de franchissement vers Sebta et Melilla : Le Maroc renforce son dispositif sécuritaire
items.description: Les autorités marocaines ont élevé leur niveau de vigilance aux abords de Ceuta et Melilla à l’approche du 15 août, date relayée par des comptes et publications d’origine inconnue appelant à des tentatives collectives de franchissement irrégulier des frontières. Les mesures déployées comprennent un renforcement des effectifs sur le terrain, la mobilisation de moyens logistiques supplémentaires ainsi que la mise en alerte d’unités spécialisées dans le maintien de l’ordre, la lutte antiémeute et la lutte contre les bandes criminelles. Parallèlement, la surveillance a été étendue aux axes routiers et aux zones côtières menant aux environs des deux enclaves espagnoles. Selon les constatations de Hespress , d’importants effectifs des forces publiques ont été mobilisés et des équipements destinés aux opérations de maintien de l’ordre acheminés dans la région. Ce dispositif, qui implique plusieurs corps sécuritaires et militaires, vise principalement à empêcher la formation de grands rassemblements à proximité des zones sensibles et à anticiper tout mouvement susceptible d’être lié aux appels diffusés sur les réseaux sociaux. Parmi les moyens déployés figurent des camions équipés de canons à eau, utilisés par les unités de maintien de l’ordre en cas de rassemblements massifs, ainsi que du matériel destiné au lancement de gaz lacrymogènes et de grenades assourdissantes. Ces équipements offrent aux forces présentes la possibilité d’intervenir à distance lorsque la situation l’exige, dans le respect des règles encadrant l’usage de la force et selon une gradation adaptée aux réalités du terrain. Aux côtés des unités antiémeute, des brigades spécialisées dans la lutte contre les bandes criminelles ont également été intégrées au dispositif de préparation. Des éléments de ces unités ont été mobilisés afin de faire face à d’éventuels actes de violence ou agressions pouvant accompagner des tentatives de passage collectif. Leur mission consiste notamment à intervenir dans les situations dépassant le cadre de simples rassemblements et à sécuriser les opérations conduites par les forces chargées du maintien de l’ordre public. D’après les informations recueillies par Hespress , le plan opérationnel ne repose pas uniquement sur un déploiement aux abords des points de passage frontaliers. Il prévoit également une surveillance élargie des axes menant aux zones frontalières, avec le maintien de postes de contrôle et d’inspection ainsi qu’un suivi des déplacements susceptibles de déboucher sur des regroupements soudains. L’objectif est d’intervenir en amont, avant que ces mouvements n’atteignent les secteurs les plus sensibles, sans concentrer les moyens sur un seul point ou un seul itinéraire. La mise en œuvre de ces mesures associe les services de la Sûreté nationale, les Forces auxiliaires et la Gendarmerie royale, chacun dans son domaine de compétence, ainsi que les Forces armées royales dans les zones relevant de leur champ d’intervention. La surveillance couvre également le littoral afin de prévenir d’éventuelles tentatives d’accès à Ceuta ou Melilla par voie maritime plutôt que terrestre. L’approche retenue repose sur une répartition des missions entre les différentes unités déployées, tout en préservant une capacité de redéploiement rapide des effectifs et des moyens en fonction de l’évolution de la situation. Certaines formations sont chargées de surveiller les mouvements dans les zones périphériques, tandis que les forces de maintien de l’ordre sont positionnées de manière à pouvoir intervenir rapidement en cas de besoin. Les unités spécialisées demeurent, pour leur part, prêtes à faire face à tout acte de violence ou d’agression constaté sur le terrain. Plus tôt dans la journée de mercredi, des sources locales et des organisations de défense des droits humains avaient indiqué à Hespress un renforcement de la présence sécuritaire dans plusieurs régions du nord du Royaume. Elles avaient également relevé un durcissement des contrôles sur les routes menant aux environs de Sebta et Melilla. Jusqu’aux premières heures de la mise en œuvre de ces mesures, aucun mouvement collectif significatif impliquant des migrants marocains ou des mineurs n’avait été observé. En revanche, quelques déplacements limités de migrants originaires d’Afrique subsaharienne ont été signalés. Ces dispositions opérationnelles s’accompagnent d’un suivi étroit des appels diffusés dans l’espace numérique. Au cours des derniers jours, le ministère de l’Intérieur a repéré des publications et messages anonymes encourageant l’organisation de tentatives collectives de franchissement irrégulier des frontières le 15 août. Les autorités estiment que ces appels sont susceptibles de mettre en danger la sécurité des participants et de provoquer des troubles à l’ordre public. S’exprimant ce mercredi 12 août à Rabat, le porte-parole officiel du ministère de l’Intérieur, Rachid El Khalfi, a affirmé que les autorités publiques avaient mobilisé l’ensemble des moyens nécessaires pour faire face à toute tentative de passage irrégulier vers Ceuta et Melilla et empêcher la participation à de telles actions. Il a également précisé que des mesures légales seraient prises à l’encontre de toute personne dont l’implication dans des actes contraires à la loi serait établie. « Les autorités suivent la situation de très près », a déclaré Rachid El Khalfi. Selon lui, les mesures adoptées comprennent l’interception des personnes cherchant à prendre part aux tentatives de franchissement, ainsi que la poursuite des individus qui en assurent la promotion sur les réseaux sociaux. Il a ajouté que les responsabilités pénales seraient engagées à l’encontre de toute personne impliquée dans des actes réprimés par la loi. Le ministère de l’Intérieur a par ailleurs annoncé l’interpellation de plusieurs individus soupçonnés d’être impliqués dans des activités d’incitation liées à ces appels. Ceux-ci ont été placés sous enquête judiciaire sous la supervision du parquet compétent. Le ministère a également souligné que le niveau de préparation sécuritaire dans les zones proches de Ceuta et Melilla ne se limite pas à la seule échéance du 15 août, mais s’inscrit dans un dispositif de vigilance permanente, ajusté en fonction des risques et des mouvements observés sur le terrain. Malawi make history, reach first-ever WAFCON final after beating Algeria 3-1
items.description: Malawi have reached their first-ever Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) final after defeating Algeria 3-1 in a thrilling semi-final in Rabat on Wednesday. The Scorchers secured the historic victory at the Olympic Stadium in Morocco, continuing their remarkable run in their debut appearance at the continental tournament. The match was a high-intensity contest, with both sides reduced to 10 players after receiving red cards during the first half. The first dismissal came early in the game, before Algeria were also shown a red card roughly 20 minutes later as the physical battle intensified. Despite playing with a reduced number of players, Malawi maintained their composure and eventually pulled away from their North African opponents to secure a 3-1 victory. The result marks another landmark achievement for Malawi, who had already secured qualification for their first-ever FIFA Women’s World Cup after reaching the semi-finals. CAF had noted ahead of the match that neither Malawi nor Algeria had previously reached a WAFCON final, meaning the winner would make history by becoming the seventh different nation to reach the final since the competition adopted its current format in 1998. Malawi had reached the last four after defeating Ghana 2-1 in the quarter-finals, a result that also secured their place at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. Their victory over Algeria now takes their extraordinary debut campaign one step further, with the Scorchers set to contest their first continental final. items.title: Eyipe’s sanitation crisis raises concerns over public health and coastal pollution
items.description: Residents of Eyipe, a community in Winneba in the Central Region, are raising concerns over persistent sanitation challenges, including improper waste disposal, open defecation and the poor management of wastewater. The situation has become particularly worrying because of the community’s proximity to the sea. Rubbish can be found in parts of the community, especially around the shoreline, while wastewater from households is sometimes discharged into open areas where waste has already accumulated. For residents, the problem goes beyond the appearance of their surroundings. They are concerned about the possible effects on public health and the coastal environment. Waste disposal remains a challenge Some residents say the cost of waste collection contributes to improper waste disposal in the community. According to them, some households struggle to pay the waste levy regularly and resort to disposing of rubbish in open spaces, sometimes early in the morning. Residents also expressed concerns about wastewater from washing and other household activities being discharged into open areas. In some locations, the wastewater mixes with accumulated rubbish, creating unhygienic conditions. The situation is more concerning around the shoreline, where some residents say rubbish is dumped close to the sea. With the community located near the coast, residents fear that continued dumping could contribute to marine pollution and affect the environment and people who depend on the sea. Residents express frustration Some residents said they had reported the sanitation problem several times but had seen limited improvement. Others declined to speak about the issue, explaining that they had raised similar concerns in the past without seeing enough action. For these residents, the problem has therefore become more than the presence of rubbish. It has also created a sense of frustration over whether their concerns are receiving adequate attention. Assembly acknowledges sanitation problem The Assembly Member for the area, Hon. Kofi Kumi, acknowledged that sanitation remains a challenge in Eyipe. He said the community does not have enough dustbins to provide residents with adequate facilities for proper waste disposal. He also identified the absence of Zoomlion waste collection services as another challenge, saying the lack of regular collection makes it difficult to manage waste generated by households. Despite these challenges, he said community clean-up exercises are organised regularly and residents are encouraged to participate. However, residents say the clean-up exercises provide only temporary relief because the community continues to face difficulties with regular waste collection and disposal. Public health concerns The sanitation situation has also raised concerns about the health of residents. A sanitation officer who spoke about the situation presented records of cholera and diarrhoea cases and explained the health risks associated with poor sanitation. Improper waste disposal and open defecation can create conditions that increase the spread of disease. For residents living near areas where rubbish accumulates, sanitation is therefore a public health issue as much as an environmental one. Concerns over coastal pollution Eyipe’s proximity to the sea adds another dimension to the sanitation challenge. Waste dumped near the shoreline and wastewater discharged carelessly can eventually enter the marine environment, raising concerns about coastal pollution and its potential impact on marine life. The situation also threatens the cleanliness of an environment that supports the livelihoods and daily activities of people in the community. Calls for a lasting solution The sanitation challenges in Eyipe are linked to several factors, including improper waste disposal, the cost of waste collection, inadequate disposal facilities and limited regular waste collection services. Addressing the situation will therefore require more than periodic clean-up exercises. Residents need access to adequate waste bins, reliable waste collection services and affordable disposal options. Continuous public education could also encourage households to adopt safer waste disposal practices. The concerns about open defecation further highlight the need for access to suitable toilet facilities and sustained sanitation education. For residents, the ultimate goal is not simply to have a clean community immediately after a clean-up exercise. They want a system that keeps the community clean throughout the year. As Eyipe continues to confront its sanitation challenges, the issue has become a reminder that public health and environmental protection are closely connected. For a community located beside the sea, addressing poor sanitation is not only about improving the appearance of the community. It is about protecting residents, preserving the coastline and ensuring a healthier environment for future generations. By Daniella Adoma Sarpong

items.title: My studio caught fire after I ignored God’s warning to ditch secular music – Perez Musik
items.description: Gospel musician Perez Musik has recounted how a fire that destroyed his recording studio became a turning point in his decision to leave secular music and focus on his Christian faith. Speaking on The Career Trail on Joy Learning TV and Joy News, Perez Musik said he had received what he described as several prophetic warnings to turn away from secular music, but continued recording artistes at his studio. “I had been getting prophecies that you need to start doing the work of God and I’ve been stubborn. Because I was enjoying the secular, recording the boys in the area. Article Wan and all. They used to come to my studio to record,” he recalled. He said the studio was later destroyed by fire after he had invested money in new equipment. Perez Musik recalled receiving money for his work as a sound engineer on Anita Erskine’s Fashion 101 . He decided to use part of the money to upgrade his studio. According to him, he had an uneasy feeling before purchasing the equipment but proceeded with the purchase. “Just when I stepped into the shop, I heard a voice. ‘So these equipment that you’re going to buy, if it catches fire and everything gets burned, what will you do?’ But I still went ahead and bought the equipment,” he said. He said the studio caught fire on 24 December. “I woke up in the morning, everything was fine. I was just going to pick something. I came back, the studio was on fire,” he recalled. Although the incident was painful, Perez Musik said he came to regard it as a turning point in his life. “It realigned my thinking. It changed my perspective on life. That, you know, material things are not things that you can hold on to. There’s something higher. There’s something greater. There’s something more, which is Christ,” he said. He subsequently became more involved in church activities, prayer and Bible study. He also said he quit drinking and smoking as he took his Christian faith more seriously. Perez Musik said he had long believed he possessed a prophetic gift but had resisted the responsibility he associated with it. “I knew the gift was there. It’s just that I was shying away from the responsibility and the requirement that comes with the gift,” he said. His spiritual transformation eventually influenced his music. “Then I started doing the urban gospel. My first album, Tenacity , was an urban gospel. So that was when everything started. From there it’s been one song after the other,” he said. He also explained how he adopted the name Perez, drawing inspiration from the biblical account of Tamar and Judah in Genesis. Perez said the name represented breakthrough and reflected what he regarded as his transition from his previous lifestyle into a new one centred on his faith.

items.title: The trouble with being online all the time
items.description: The growing amount of time people spend on smartphones and social media is raising concerns about its impact on attention, relationships and everyday life, particularly among young people. For many, checking a phone has become part of almost every daily activity. People scroll through social media while eating, wait for messages while studying and turn to their phones whenever they have a few moments of free time. What may appear to be a harmless habit can gradually become difficult to control. Psychologists and digital-wellbeing experts have increasingly warned that excessive screen use can affect people’s ability to concentrate and remain present in their daily lives. Constant notifications and the pressure to respond can also make it difficult for people to disconnect. Social media adds another dimension to the problem. Platforms are designed to keep users engaged by constantly providing new content. Users can spend hours viewing carefully selected images and videos showing other people’s achievements, holidays and lifestyles. This can encourage unhealthy comparisons, particularly when people compare their everyday lives with the carefully edited versions of other people’s lives presented online. The issue is not that technology itself is harmful. Smartphones and the internet have transformed communication, education, business and access to information. The challenge is finding a healthy balance between digital activity and real-world interaction. For some people, that balance begins with simple changes. Putting phones away during meals, turning off unnecessary notifications and taking regular breaks from social media can create opportunities for people to focus on their surroundings and interact with others without digital distractions. Taking a walk without constantly checking a phone can also provide an opportunity to think, observe and enjoy the environment. There is also growing recognition that boredom is not necessarily a bad thing. Having periods without constant entertainment can give people time to reflect, develop ideas and engage in activities that require creativity. For young people especially, developing healthy digital habits may be important as smartphones and social media become increasingly integrated into education, work and social life. The solution, therefore, may not be to abandon technology but to use it more deliberately. The internet is unlikely to disappear, and social media will remain an important part of modern communication. However, individuals can decide how much control these platforms have over their time and attention. The challenge is to remain connected without becoming so connected that the real world is forgotten. Sometimes, putting the phone down may be the first step towards noticing what has been happening around us all along.
