items.title: Éclipse solaire : les bons réflexes pour observer le phénomène sans danger
items.description: Une éclipse solaire constitue un phénomène astronomique spectaculaire, susceptible de susciter la curiosité de nombreux observateurs. Mais si le rendez-vous céleste peut être admiré, il ne doit surtout pas l’être au mépris des précautions nécessaires. À l’occasion de l’éclipse solaire, le ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique appelle les populations à protéger leurs yeux et à redoubler de vigilance, notamment à l’égard des enfants. Le Soleil, un danger pour les yeux Contrairement à une idée répandue, la diminution apparente de la luminosité du Soleil pendant une éclipse ne le rend pas moins dangereux pour la vision. Regarder directement le Soleil, même brièvement et sans protection adaptée, peut provoquer des lésions importantes de la rétine. La particularité de ces atteintes est qu’elles peuvent apparaître sans douleur immédiate. Dans certains cas, elles peuvent entraîner une baisse de la vision susceptible d’être irréversible. Des équipements adaptés indispensables Pour observer directement une éclipse, les autorités sanitaires recommandent exclusivement l’utilisation de lunettes spécialement conçues pour l’observation des éclipses solaires et conformes aux normes de sécurité en vigueur. Les lunettes de soleil classiques, même très foncées, ne constituent pas une protection suffisante. Il est également déconseillé d’utiliser des solutions improvisées telles que les verres teintés, les films photographiques, les radiographies ou d’autres filtres artisanaux. Une vigilance particulière est également requise avec les instruments optiques. Jumelles, télescopes, appareils photo et autres dispositifs ne doivent jamais être utilisés pour regarder le Soleil sans un filtre solaire spécifiquement adapté. Les enfants particulièrement concernés Les enfants doivent faire l’objet d’une surveillance accrue pendant le phénomène. Il est recommandé de leur expliquer les risques liés à l’observation directe du Soleil et de les accompagner s’ils souhaitent suivre l’éclipse. Pour les personnes qui ne disposent pas d’un équipement répondant aux exigences de sécurité, le choix le plus prudent reste de ne pas regarder directement le Soleil. Rester attentif après l’éclipse La vigilance doit se poursuivre après le phénomène. Une atteinte rétinienne peut ne provoquer aucune douleur au moment de l’exposition. Certains symptômes peuvent toutefois apparaître dans les heures qui suivent : vision floue, baisse de la vision, apparition d’une tache sombre ou d’une zone floue au centre du champ visuel, déformation des images ou sensibilité inhabituelle à la lumière. En cas d’apparition de l’un de ces signes après avoir regardé le Soleil, il est recommandé de consulter rapidement un professionnel de santé spécialisé en ophtalmologie. L’éclipse ne dure que quelques instants, mais les dommages qu’une observation imprudente peut provoquer sur la vision peuvent, eux, être durables. La prudence reste donc la meilleure manière de profiter de ce spectacle astronomique.

items.title: Labé : Un «fou » interpellé avec des dollars et plusieurs téléphones
items.description: Portant des habits usés et faisant croire à des troubles mentaux, un homme aux agissements suspects a été arrêté ce mercredi 12 août à Labé en possession de 700 dollars américains et de plusieurs téléphones. Pris en chasse par la vigilance des citoyens, le suspect est désormais au cœur d'une enquête d'une sensibilité inattendue, a appris la rédaction régionale de Guinéenews basée à Labé. C’est une scène pour le moins inhabituelle qui s’est déroulée à quelques mètres seulement du commissariat central de police de Labé, au carrefour Tinkisso. Un individu au profil énigmatique, que beaucoup prenaient jusqu'ici pour un simple déficient mental, a été interpellé ce mercredi 12 août 2026 par les agents de la police centrale. La vigilance des chauffeurs de taxi-moto de la zone a été le facteur déclencheur. Intrigués par le comportement suspect de l'homme, ces derniers ont commencé à l'encercler et à s'interroger ouvertement sur ses faits et gestes. Sentant le piège se refermer et redoutant la vindicte populaire, l'inconnu a préféré se réfugier de lui-même auprès des forces de l'ordre. La fouille de ses effets personnels a révélé une surprise de taille : sous ses vêtements usés, l'homme dissimulait la somme de 700 dollars américains, plusieurs téléphones portables et divers objets. Cette arrestation ravive de sombres souvenirs dans la cité de Karamoko Alpha. Selon les informations recueillies par nos reporters, l'individu n'en est pas à son coup d'essai. Il avait déjà été appréhendé il y a quelque temps aux alentours de la gare routière de Kouroula pour une affaire de vol. Mory Diakité, secrétaire général du syndicat des taxis-motos USTG (union syndicale des travailleurs de Guinée) de Labé, se souvient très bien de cet épisode : « À l'époque, il avait été saisi avec un lot d'objets suspects, dont de nombreuses cartes SIM. Malheureusement, tout le monde avait conclu qu'il s'agissait d'un fou et il avait été libéré sans que l'on cherche à comprendre comment il s'était procuré toutes ces puces », déplore-t-il. Si le commissariat central de Labé se refuse pour l'instant à tout commentaire officiel, l'affaire a pris une tournure judiciaire et politique majeure. Selon des sources concordantes, le procureur près le tribunal de première instance (TPI) de Labé ainsi que sa hiérarchie ont immédiatement été saisis. Plus évocateur encore : le dossier serait suivi de très près jusqu'au niveau de la Présidence de la République. Aux dernières nouvelles, dès la fin des enquêtes préliminaires menées par les services locaux, le suspect devrait être transféré sous haute escorte vers Conakry pour la suite des investigations. Dans la ville de Labé, l'incompréhension laisse place aux spéculations : s'agit-il d'un réseau d'espionnage, de grand banditisme ou de trafic organisé utilisant la folie comme couverture ? Les résultats de l'enquête sont attendus dans les jours à venir. A suivre

items.title: AJK polls: Rathore’s LA-17 Haveli victory disputed, local PML-N announces indefinite strike
items.description: MUZAFFARABAD: A controversy emerged on Wednesday after the returning officer (RO) issued Form 27 declaring PPP’s Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, the sitting AJK prime minister, the winner from LA-17 (Haveli), despite rival PML-N candidate Engineer Mohsin Aziz being assured that the form would not be issued until the Election Commission took up his complaint. The development triggered fresh tensions in Haveli district, where PML-N workers announced a complete shutter-down strike and protest from Thursday (August 13) for an indefinite period. At a meeting in Forward Kahuta, chaired by PML-N Haveli president Syed Abid Bukhari, participants demanded that the Election Commission open all polling bags from LA-17, order a recount and determine the result on the basis of the original results issued by presiding officers at the polling stations. They warned that the scope of the protest would be expanded if the demand was not accepted. Polling in the constituency had been held on Monday amid serious allegations and counter-allegations of rigging by all three major contestants — PM Rathore of PPP, PML-N’s Aziz and independent candidate Khawaja Tariq Saeed. Late on Monday evening, thousands of Aziz’s supporters gathered at the district courts, claiming that the results provided to polling agents by presiding officers on Form 24 showed their candidate leading Rathore by more than 8,000 votes, but that the RO was subsequently preparing the result in favour of the prime minister. There were also reports of some people being injured during the demonstration. The protest ended on Tuesday after Aziz said in a video message that the RO had given him a written undertaking that Form 27 would not be issued until the Election Commission in Muzaffarabad decided his claim. On Tuesday, Chief Election Commissioner Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal had told Dawn that the Commission would take a decision after the polling bags and relevant election records reached its office. He had reportedly given a similar assurance to Aziz over the phone. The DRO, Waheed Mughal, and RO, Asheer Chughtai, both members of the subordinate judiciary, were evacuated from their offices in Forward Kahuta along with the polling bags with the help of the army’s Quick Response Force (QRF). They reached Muzaffarabad by midnight. However, the RO subsequently issued Form 27 after midnight, dated August 11, declaring Rathore the winner with 33,872 votes. Aziz secured 32,354 votes, followed by Saeed with 12,538 and IPP candidate Amir Nazir Chaudhry with 5,405. Hours later, PM Rathore said on X that his “remarkable victory had been officially notified”. “LA-17 has spoken. I thank the people of Haveli and again pledge to serve them now and forever. I’m grateful to my party leadership, specially, Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari and Adi Faryal Talpur, for their trust, guidance and unending support amid every challenge we have faced,” he wrote. The issuance of Form 27, however, failed to settle the dispute, with reports from Haveli suggesting that tensions were rising again. In a video message recorded in Muzaffarabad, Aziz reiterated his allegation that the Form 24s handed to polling agents of all nine participating candidates contained the genuine results, while different figures were subsequently taken into consideration by the RO. He offered to have just two polling bags, rather than all of them, opened from areas where he alleged the results had been changed. If his allegation proved to be wrong, he said, he would apologise and congratulate Rathore. “If Faisal Rathore has won, why is he afraid of opening of polling bags and a subsequent recount?” he asked. Aziz also claimed that the Election Act, 2020, made it obligatory for the RO to open polling bags following a complaint by any candidate. He said that when they asked Chughtai to take the step, the RO maintained that he was unaware of the provision and did not have a copy of the Act with him. On Wednesday, senior lawyers Raja Sajjad Ahmed and Chaudhry Ghulam Nabi submitted an application to the chief election commissioner, seeking a recount of votes polled in LA-17 over alleged tampering with the results. The Election Commission announced that it would take up the matter at 10am on Thursday. In a post on X, PML-N leader and federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry called for a transparent investigation into the rigging complaint filed by Aziz, saying he hoped the Election Commission would address the allegations regarding the Haveli constituency on merit. Aziz, however, said he had little hope from the commission after what he described as its failure to prevent the issuance of the “unlawful Form 27”. “I will take my case to the people’s court apart from the superior judiciary,” he said. Meanwhile, Saeed also alleged tampering with his results and called for a recount. He claimed that he had won at nine polling stations, but the votes secured by him there had not been included in his tally and had instead been added to that of Rathore. PPP calls polls ‘rigged and violent’ Against this backdrop, the PPP also criticised the conduct of the AJK elections, with a high-level meeting of the party in Islamabad describing the polls as “rigged and violent” and expressing serious concern over the role of the AJK Election Commission. The meeting, chaired by PPP Women’s Wing president and AJK affairs in-charge Faryal Talpur, also criticised the phase-wise conduct of the elections and demanded the immediate completion of polling in the remaining two districts of the third phase and seven constituencies of Poonch so that the Legislative Assembly could be fully constituted. The participants raised questions over the suspension of internet services, shortages of polling material and staff at some polling stations, and alleged inadequate security arrangements. Talpur said the PPP was the representative party of the people of AJK and had continued to enjoy strong public support despite challenging circumstances. On the other hand, Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the PML-N had secured a clear lead in the elections and would have 24 general seats, with another six reserved seats, taking its strength to 30. In his post on X, he said the AJK Assembly session would be convened next week for the swearing-in of members and election of reserved seats, followed by elections for the speaker and prime minister. Chaudhry described the elections as free, fair and credible, saying there had been “zero tolerance” for misconduct or rigging. He cited the arrest of a candidate in LA-6 (Mirpur) for taking away a ballot box from a polling station as an example of action against electoral misconduct.

items.title: Hamdallah et Ronaldo à la poursuite d’Al-Somah : la bataille des buteurs s’annonce explosive
items.description: À quelques jours du coup d’envoi de la 19e saison du championnat saoudien, la course au titre de meilleur buteur historique promet déjà d’être passionnante. En tête depuis plusieurs années, le Syrien Omar Al-Somah voit le Marocain Abderrazak Hamdallah se rapprocher dangereusement, tandis que Cristiano Ronaldo continue de grimper dans la hiérarchie. Le championnat saoudien ne se joue pas uniquement pour le titre. À chaque saison, les stars de la Saudi Pro League se livrent également une bataille acharnée pour inscrire leur nom dans l’histoire de la compétition. Et dans cette course, Abderrazak Hamdallah est le principal poursuivant d’Omar Al-Somah. L’ancien attaquant d’Al-Ahli et d’Al-Hilal reste le meilleur buteur de l’histoire du championnat saoudien avec 161 réalisations. Mais son record est désormais sérieusement menacé par l’international marocain. Auteur de 156 buts en championnat saoudien, Hamdallah n’est plus qu’à cinq longueurs d’Al-Somah. Le Marocain, aujourd’hui attaquant de Al-Taawoun FC, pourrait donc s’emparer du record dès cette saison s’il conserve son efficacité devant le but. Arrivé en Arabie saoudite en 2018, Hamdallah s’est rapidement imposé comme l’un des attaquants les plus prolifiques de l’histoire de la Saudi Pro League. Son instinct dans la surface et sa régularité lui permettent aujourd’hui de viser un nouveau record individuel. Derrière le Marocain, une autre superstar continue de faire parler ses statistiques : Cristiano Ronaldo. Le capitaine d’Al-Nassr compte désormais 102 buts en championnat saoudien. Il a atteint ce total lors de la dernière journée de la saison passée, face à Damac. En seulement quelques saisons, le Portugais a donc déjà intégré le cercle très fermé des joueurs ayant inscrit plus de 100 buts dans la compétition. À l’aube de cette nouvelle saison, tous les regards seront donc tournés vers Abderrazak Hamdallah. Avec seulement cinq buts à inscrire pour égaler Al-Somah, puis six pour devenir le meilleur buteur de l’histoire du championnat saoudien, l’attaquant marocain a une occasion en or d’entrer définitivement dans la légende. Et derrière lui, Cristiano Ronaldo poursuit sa propre ascension. La nouvelle saison pourrait ainsi offrir une bataille spectaculaire entre plusieurs générations de buteurs. items.title: Voter apathy: Youth silence is killing democracy — PDP
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, has warned that voter apathy among young Nigerians is weakening the country’s democracy, urging youths to convert their numerical strength into electoral power by actively participating in elections and governance. The warning came yesterday in Abuja at the party’s 2026 International Youth Day programme, where speakers said young Nigerians could no longer afford to remain spectators in decisions shaping their future. They identified voter apathy, unemployment, economic hardship and the high cost of political participation as major obstacles to youth involvement. Delivering the keynote address, PDP National Director of Administration, Arthur Ekwelem, said Nigeria’s youths had the numbers, energy, creativity and digital influence to transform the electoral landscape. “Democracy thrives on participation. When citizens withdraw from the electoral process, they surrender part of their democratic power to others,” Ekwelem said. He identified distrust in political leaders and institutions, fear of electoral violence, economic hardship, misinformation, inadequate civic education and logistical difficulties among the factors discouraging citizens from voting. Representing the Chairman of the occasion, former Jigawa State governor, Sule Lamido, the PDP Gombe governorship candidate, Isah Pantami, said youths, who constitute more than 60 per cent of Nigeria’s population, must have a stronger voice in policymaking and governance. “They are the backbone of our humanity. They are the vanguards of any positive change. They are the ambassadors of progress and development,” Pantami said. He listed opportunities in the creative industry, digital economy, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, smart agriculture and other emerging sectors, but said unemployment, an outdated education system, inadequate mentorship and the rising cost of living were limiting young Nigerians. Pantami also criticised the gap between the ‘Not Too Young To Run’ principle and the realities of seeking elective office, saying nomination fees, campaigns and other election expenses had made political participation difficult for many youths. “Not too young to run … is only about an academic work where we have a law in place,” he said. Director-General of the PDP Female Youth Wing, Hon. Loveth Izekor, urged young women to move beyond being mobilised for elections and become decision-makers. “Democracy dies when youth are silent. We must move from being mobilised to being decision-makers,” Izekor said. She called for greater access to political funding, training and tickets for young women, saying the gathering was intended as a strategy session rather than merely a celebration. PDP National Youth Leader, Amb. Ibrahim Bala-Aboki, said his office had focused on youth mobilisation, inclusion and grassroots participation since assuming office, including mobilising young members for party congresses, INEC e-registration and elective positions. He said the PDP had also inaugurated a National Youth Leadership Consultative Forum and commenced the revalidation of youth support groups nationwide. Bala-Aboki announced a skills programme to train 100 youths as trainers, with each expected to train 50 youths across the country’s 774 local government areas in vocational and entrepreneurial skills. “This is the time for action, not docility; time for valued alacrity, not void alarms; time for greater momentum, not murmurs,” he said. He urged young Nigerians to reject voter apathy, insisting that their numerical strength could determine the direction of Nigerian democracy. “Every voter is a leader. Together, let us shape and forge our chosen future,” Bala-Aboki said. The post Voter apathy: Youth silence is killing democracy — PDP appeared first on Vanguard News .

Osun Election: Act now, don’t wait until after the damage – Accord tells EU
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Accord Party has appealed to the European Union, EU, to urgently deploy preventive diplomacy to ease mounting political tension in Osun State ahead of Saturday’s governorship election, warning that international action after violence or electoral damage would come too late. With the August 15 poll only days away, the party said the growing reports of violence, intimidation, arrests and alleged partisan use of state institutions were creating an atmosphere in which political parties and voters could lose confidence in the electoral process. It said the outcome would also matter beyond Osun, as the election is the last major off-cycle governorship contest before the 2027 general election. Accord National Chairman, Chief Maxwell Mgbudem, made the appeal in a letter dated August 12 and addressed to the EU Ambassador and Head of Delegation to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Migot. “We believe that the present situation calls for preventive diplomacy rather than intervention after the damage has been done,” Mgbudem said. Accord alleged that at least 29 people had lost their lives in incidents connected with the political environment in Osun, while several others sustained gunshot injuries. It also claimed that more than 60 of its members and supporters were arrested and detained in Abuja and Nasarawa State, and called for the circumstances surrounding the arrests to be independently scrutinised. The party said the arrests were part of a wider pattern of actions that, in its view, had heightened anxiety among political actors and residents as the election approaches. It also raised concerns over searches of the residences of senior Osun Government officials and the arrest and detention of some officials, including the Secretary to the State Government. Although the officials were subsequently released following widespread public concern, Accord said the circumstances surrounding their arrests still required transparent clarification. The party cited the reported freezing of Osun State Government bank accounts by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, and President Bola Tinubu’s subsequent directive for the accounts to be unfrozen after public criticism, as another development that had fuelled concerns about the perceived use of state institutions during the election period. Accord, however, acknowledged the constitutional and statutory duties of law-enforcement and anti-corruption agencies, stressing that its objection was not to lawful investigations or enforcement. “Our concern, therefore, is not to obstruct any lawful investigation or enforcement action, but to ensure that legitimate State powers are not deployed in a manner that intimidates political opponents, restricts lawful political participation or creates an uneven electoral playing field,” the party said. Mgbudem also drew the EU’s attention to what Accord described as attacks, harassment and intimidation directed at its members, particularly a viral video which, according to the party, showed a sitting senator ordering that Accord members be killed wherever they were found. Accord said the alleged threat, whether intended or otherwise, could weaken the party’s ability to mobilise and participate effectively in the election. It urged the EU to encourage Nigerian authorities to ensure that no party, candidate or citizen is disadvantaged through the selective application of state power or misuse of public institutions. Specifically, the party asked the EU to publicly reaffirm the need for a free, fair, transparent, credible and peaceful election in which the outcome reflects the freely expressed will of Osun voters. It also urged political parties, candidates and supporters to reject violence, intimidation, inflammatory rhetoric, hate speech and political provocation, while calling on the Federal Government, security agencies and other public institutions to remain politically neutral and professional throughout the electoral process. Accord further urged the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to discharge its constitutional and statutory responsibilities independently, impartially and transparently, in line with the Constitution, Electoral Act and relevant regulations. It called on security and law-enforcement agencies to operate within the law and respect fundamental rights and due process, particularly in the tense period immediately before and after the election. The party also sought credible domestic and international observation of the poll, including mechanisms for documenting incidents that could threaten its integrity or peaceful conduct. It urged political actors to accept the legitimate outcome while pursuing genuine grievances through established legal channels, and called for accountability against anyone credibly established to have sponsored, perpetrated or facilitated political violence or electoral intimidation, irrespective of political affiliation. Accord said the EU could help prevent further deterioration by encouraging restraint and dialogue among political actors before the situation becomes harder to contain. “A timely and principled intervention by the European Union could send a powerful message that political competition must remain peaceful, democratic and respectful of the rule of law,” it said. The party described Saturday’s election as more than a contest for political office, saying it would test Nigeria’s ability to conduct an election in which institutions remain neutral, political parties compete on a level playing field and voters exercise their franchise without fear. It warned that a peaceful, transparent and credible poll would strengthen confidence in Nigeria’s democratic institutions ahead of 2027, while any perception that violence, intimidation, institutional bias or manipulation influenced the outcome could further erode public trust. “We are not asking the European Union to take sides in the political contest or to endorse any political party or candidate. Our appeal is for the protection of democratic principles, the rule of law, political pluralism and the fundamental right of the people of Osun State to freely choose their leaders,” Accord said. The party said its appeal was ultimately about ensuring that the people of Osun State, rather than fear, intimidation or institutional pressure, determine their political future through a peaceful, transparent and credible electoral process. The post Osun Election: Act now, don’t wait until after the damage – Accord tells EU appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Major Russian grain export terminal hit in Ukraine Black Sea port attack
items.description: A “massive” Ukrainian drone and missile strike on Russia’s port city of Novorossiysk has damaged grain export terminals and hit the last major Russian naval base on the Black Sea. Three people, including an eight-year-old child, were killed and 24 people were injured in the Wednesday nighttime attack. Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed Ukraine had launched rocket and underwater drones in a “unique operation” to strike the Russian naval base at Novorossiysk, although he did not mention grain terminals being hit. “The occupying fleet and all the infrastructure that supports it will not be safe as long as Russian aggression continues,” Zelensky said. Most of Russia’s Black Sea fleet is docked in Novorossiysk – one of the largest ports in Russia – after it was forced to vacate its former home base of Sevastopol, in the Russia-occupied Crimean peninsula, which was too exposed to Ukrainian attacks. A major grain trading company confirmed to Russia’s TASS news agency that its terminal had been hit, while another told Reuters and Russian outlet RBK the same. The Russian agriculture ministry announced on Wednesday that it was working to redirect cargo flows to ports in the Baltic and Caspian Seas as well as land routes. It did not make any reference to Ukraine’s attacks but said it was “taking into account current logistical constraints”. Repeated explosions reportedly rang out over Novorossiysk throughout the night as air defences shot down aerial objects. An emergency situation was declared in the city on Wednesday, after the barrage of drones struck areas around the port and damaged pipelines, suspending water supply for the city. Elsewhere in the region a man was killed by drone debris, Regional Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said. Several locations in the surrounding Krasnodar region were also struck by “several hundred drones” overnight, Kondratyev added, with dozens of buildings damaged, including homes. For its part, Moscow launched aerial strikes which killed at least 11 civilians overnight between Tuesday and Wednesday. The majority were killed when Russia hit the city of Zaporizhzhia with ballistic missiles and glide bombs. Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. After a period of relative calm in the Black Sea, over the course of this summer Kyiv and Moscow resumed striking one another’s ports and shipping. The last remaining sea route out of Ukraine has been badly affected by several deadly Russian strikes on cargo ships and the port of Odesa, through which Moscow seeks to put off foreign companies from trading with Ukraine. In July, the Ukrainian Agribusiness Club (UCAB) reported a 23% decrease in exports. Meanwhile, Ukraine has grown increasingly adept at carrying out long-range strikes on Russian territory. Its recent attacks on vessels in the eastern Black Sea have disrupted Russia’s grain shipments, too. Russia is the world’s largest wheat exporter – but according to a Moscow-based analytics company, exports for August could fall by more than half compared to the same month over the last five years due to the disruption in the Black and Azov seas. On Wednesday, Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova accused Ukraine of carrying out strikes on Russian grain and agricultural infrastructure, resulting in a hike in global food prices and growing grain shortages. But Zakharova also said that for its part Russia would continue striking “facilities that [Ukraine’s armed forces] use on the Black Sea to destabilise the navigation situation” until “the full elimination of threats to security projected to the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea”. Concerns over how the war in Ukraine would affect global food supplies have been persistent since Moscow invaded in 2022. Together, Russia and Ukraine account for a significant share of global grain trade, particularly for buyers in North Africa, the Middle East and parts of Asia. The 2022 Black Sea Grain Initiative, under which Russia agreed to lift its blockade on Ukraine’s agricultural exports, did not last after Moscow resumed attacks on vessels using the maritime corridors to Odesa the following year.

items.title: LA Lakers to be sold in record $12.5bn deal
items.description: The Los Angeles Lakers are to be sold for a reported record-breaking $12.5bn, external (£9.3bn) – less than a year after Mark Walter took a majority stake in the NBA franchise. Josh Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared, and former Disney chief executive Bob Iger are buying the controlling interest in one of the world’s most iconic sports teams. Walter bought his share, reportedly worth an estimated $10bn (£7.45bn) – a previous record – from the Buss family in a deal that was unanimously approved by the NBA Board of Governors in October 2025. Kushner and Iger said in a statement: “As lifelong NBA fans, we are deeply honoured for the opportunity to become stewards of the Los Angeles Lakers, one of the most iconic sports franchises in the world. “We have immense respect for the leadership and vision of Jerry and Jeanie Buss. “Our long-term commitment is to build on that foundation, compete at the highest level, and serve this extraordinary team, its fans, and the city of Los Angeles.” Jerry Buss bought the Lakers in a $67.5m deal (£50m) in 1979 that included the Los Angeles Kings hockey team and a Los Angeles arena, known as the Kia Forum. After he died in 2013, ownership was passed to his six children in a Trust before a deal was completed with Walter, who also owns a stake in the LA Dodgers with Todd Boehly. “Owning the Los Angeles Lakers has been one of the great honors of my life,” said Walter. “It has been an extraordinary investment, but what I will carry with me is the community, the fans, and a city that treats this team as family. “I am grateful to Jeanie Buss, the Buss family, the players, and the staff for welcoming me into this chapter. The Lakers belong to Los Angeles, and I have every confidence the best is still ahead.” The LA Lakers have 17 NBA titles – one less than the record of 18 held by the Boston Celtics. The deal involving Kushner comes after he was part of the recent controversy surrounding Fifa president Gianni Infantino and an aborted plan to sell off stakes in the governing body’s competitions to private investors. Thrive Eternal, an American venture capital firm founded by Kushner, was expected to lead the proposed investor group for the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

items.title: Sixteen inmates injured after lightning strikes US prison
items.description: Lightning struck an Ohio prison during severe weather in the state on Tuesday, injuring 16 inmates, one of which had to be airlifted to hospital. The prisoners were outside during the storm, moving between buildings after an evening meal. Nine of the inmates have since returned to the correctional institution, while seven remain in hospital, including one in serious condition, the Ohio Department of Rehabilitation and Correction said. Severe weather and flash flooding has ravaged parts of the US Midwest in recent days, generating tornadoes, strong winds and causing widespread power outages. No staff were injured in the strike, the Ohio Department of Rehabilitation and Correction said in a Wednesday morning update on social media. The nature of injuries to the inmate who was airlifted from the scene has not been disclosed. BBC News has contacted the institution for comment. The lightning strike hit amid severe weather conditions across the Midwest region. The National Weather Service (NWS) has issued flash flooding warnings across Ohio and Indiana, and confirmed that three tornadoes touched down in Chicago’s south suburbs on Tuesday. Footage from across the region shows homes with damaged roofs and trees that have been downed as a result of the storms. At least three deaths have been confirmed, including that of a four-year-old boy whose family’s mobile home in Indiana was struck by a tree. An Indiana woman was killed in a home explosion during a period of powerful winds of more than 100 miles (160km) per hour, according to CBS news, the BBC’s US partner. First response efforts were delayed as a result of the road conditions, said police captain Rob Maynard. He said that although they believe the storm played a role in the woman’s death, they are unable to draw final conclusions right now. There were also several gas leaks as a result of the storm, which can be caused when large trees fall and disrupt underground infrastructure, Maynard added. In Ohio, another individual died when first responders were unable to quickly reach them during a flooding emergency, said Ohio Governor Mike DeWine. “This is a very dangerous weather situation,” DeWine said on Tuesday, while warning people to keep an eye on the news and use “common sense”. The storms have caused extensive power outages across the region. More than 295,000 customers are without power in Indiana, as well as more than 185,000 in Ohio and 145,000 in Illinois, according to a power tracker webpage on Wednesday. “Now is the time to plan for severe weather and flooding!” the NWS said, while warning of severe wind gusts strong enough to knock down trees, branches and power lines. The Federal Aviation Administration issued ground stops at major airports in the area due to thunderstorms, including Chicago’s O’Hare and Midway airports, which continue into Wednesday afternoon.

items.title: Tinubu, AbdulRazaq praised as new Army battalion begins operations in Kwara
items.description: Traditional rulers, community leaders and residents of Irepodun Local Government Area of Kwara State have commended President Bola Tinubu and Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq for facilitating the establishment of a Nigerian Army battalion in Omu-Aran. The stakeholders said the deployment would strengthen security in Kwara South and improve the protection of communities in the area. They spoke on Tuesday during a reception organised to welcome officers and soldiers of the new battalion, commanded by Lt.-Col. Kehinde Avoseh. The Olomu of Omu-Aran, Oba AbdulRaheem Adeoti, pledged the community’s full support for the troops and assured them of a peaceful and hospitable environment. “I want to assure you that our support, especially in terms of the welfare of the battalion, will be 100 per cent, by the grace of God. You will enjoy your stay in Omu-Aran,” Adeoti said. The monarch also expressed appreciation to the military authorities for retaining Omu-Aran as the location of the battalion, describing the development as an opportunity to promote security and progress in the community. The Chairman of Irepodun Local Government, Abdulazeez Yakub, similarly pledged the council’s cooperation with the Nigerian Army. “On behalf of the people of Irepodun Local Government, I assure you of our full cooperation and support as you carry out your duties,” he said. President of the Omu-Aran Development Association, Prince Niyi Adeyeye, said the military presence would help strengthen security in Omu-Aran and other communities across Kwara South. A retired military officer and community leader, Lasisi Abidoye, also commended Tinubu and AbdulRazaq for supporting the establishment of the battalion, promising maximum cooperation from residents. Speaking at the event, Commander of the 22 Armoured Brigade, Brig. Gen. Nicholas Rume, thanked residents for their warm reception. He said the deployment was part of the Federal Government’s plan to expand the Nigerian Army’s operational capacity across the country. items.title: Bawumia, Dumelo, Afenyo-Markin, Bola Ray, others to headline Empower Vault Summit on October 14
items.description: The annual Empower Vault Summit is set to take place on Friday, August 14, at the Great Hall of the University of Ghana. This is a high-impact leadership and mentorship platform aimed at equipping young people with the skills, values, and mindset needed to succeed. The summit is being organised by Stables and Horses in partnership with the Office of the University of Ghana SRC Vice President. The initiative is designed to provide young people across Ghana with clarity of purpose, strong personal values and practical tools for leadership, entrepreneurship and personal development. Former Vice President, Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia, is expected to attend as Guest of Honour, while a distinguished line-up of public officials, business leaders and industry personalities will engage participants throughout the event. Among the speakers are Osman Abdulai Ayariga, Chief Executive Officer of the National Youth Authority; John Dumelo; Alexander Afenyo-Markin, Minority Leader and MP for Effutu; and George Opare Addo, Minister for Youth Development and Empowerment. Other speakers include Dr. Dora Oforiwaa Hall, CEO of Zoe Dental; Bayo Adedeji; Bola Ray, CEO of EIB Network; Ewura Karim Adams; and Prof. Rosina Kyerematen, Dean of Student Affairs at the University of Ghana. The summit will also feature breakout sessions designed to give participants more intimate and practical engagement with influential voices and young personalities. These sessions will feature Endurance Grand, Nyamewaa, Willie Chembez and Asiedu Mends . A major attraction of the summit will be an entrepreneurship challenge, giving students the opportunity to pitch their businesses, present innovative ideas and compete for a GH¢10,000 cash prize. The challenge is expected to provide a platform for emerging entrepreneurs to gain visibility, receive feedback and demonstrate how their ideas can address real-world challenges. Some scholarship opportunities are also in the offing for some brilliant but needy students as part of the event. Senior Project Manager and Brand Strategist for the Empower Vault Summit, Joey Joseph Nii Ayi Otokunor, is leading the project management and strategic direction of the initiative. “We believe young people do not lack potential; what they often need is the right platform, guidance and opportunity to unlock it. Empower Vault is designed to provide exactly that—connecting young people with leaders, mentors and opportunities that can shape their next chapter,” he said. The Empower Vault Summit is expected to bring together students, young entrepreneurs, aspiring leaders, creatives and other young people seeking guidance and opportunities to accelerate their personal and professional development. The organisers say the summit forms part of a broader effort to empower young people to take ownership of their futures, develop strong leadership values and translate their ideas into tangible opportunities.

items.title: Finance islamique en Guinée : Coris Bank Baraka mise sur une offre éthique et accessible à tous
items.description: La finance islamique poursuit progressivement son implantation en Guinée et entend se positionner comme une alternative financière éthique, inclusive et adaptée aux besoins des différents acteurs économiques. C’est dans cette dynamique qu’une rencontre s’est tenue, ce mercredi 12 août 2026, dans les locaux de l’agence de Coris Bank Internationale Guinée à Kipé, à Conakry, autour des opportunités et des perspectives offertes par la finance islamique. La rencontre a permis aux participants d’échanger avec Dr Abdessattar Khouildi, expert en matière de finance islamique et président du Conseil de conformité interne de Coris Bank Internationale. Venu en Guinée pour accompagner et encadrer certaines activités liées à ce secteur, il a partagé son expertise et apporté des éclairages sur les mécanismes, les principes et les perspectives de la finance islamique. Il a notamment mis l’accent sur le caractère universel de ce modèle financier, qui, contrairement à certaines perceptions, ne s’adresse pas exclusivement aux musulmans. « La finance islamique s'adresse à tout le monde », a-t-il souligné, rappelant qu’elle repose sur des principes éthiques et des règles spécifiques, tout en étant ouverte à l’ensemble des acteurs économiques. Selon l’expert, les petites et moyennes entreprises occupent une place importante dans l’écosystème de la finance islamique. Elles peuvent bénéficier d’une gamme diversifiée de solutions destinées notamment au financement du fonds de roulement, à l’acquisition de marchandises et au financement des équipements. Une offre qui, selon lui, permet aux institutions financières islamiques d’accompagner les entreprises dans le développement et la consolidation de leurs activités. Dr Abdessattar Khouildi a toutefois relevé plusieurs défis auxquels le secteur doit faire face, notamment la nécessité de bien connaître l’environnement économique, de sélectionner une clientèle adaptée et de proposer des solutions correspondant réellement aux besoins des opérateurs. Il estime que l’innovation demeure indispensable pour permettre à la finance islamique de rester en phase avec les évolutions du marché. La question de la conformité constitue également un élément essentiel de ce modèle financier. Dans ce cadre, le rôle du Conseil de conformité interne est déterminant. Dr Khouildi a expliqué que les établissements spécialisés disposent de mécanismes permettant d’examiner les opérations, de valider les produits en amont et d’assurer leur suivi à travers des dispositifs de contrôle et d’audit. Un système destiné à renforcer la confiance des clients, aussi bien dans la gestion de leurs dépôts que dans les opérations de financement. De son côté, Fatoumata Bah, responsable de Coris Bank Internationale Guinée, a apporté des précisions sur le fonctionnement de Baraka. Elle a notamment rappelé que Coris Bank Internationale Baraka n’est pas une banque distincte, mais une fenêtre spécialisée de Coris Bank Internationale Guinée, dédiée à la commercialisation de produits et services conformes aux principes de la Charia. «Nous offrons des produits à des particuliers, des entreprises, des PME, des PMI et des associations », a-t-elle expliqué. L’offre de Baraka comprend notamment la Mourabaha et l’Ijara, présentées comme des produits phares, ainsi que les comptes Wadiah, destinés aussi bien aux particuliers qu’aux entreprises. La banque dispose également d’un conseil de conformité interne chargé de valider les produits et les contrats avant leur commercialisation. Concernant l’accès aux services, Fatoumata Bah a indiqué que les personnes intéressées peuvent se rendre dans l’une des agences du réseau de Coris Bank Internationale Guinée, présentes à Conakry et à l’intérieur du pays, afin d’ouvrir un compte Baraka. Pour les particuliers, les formalités comprennent notamment deux photos, une copie de la pièce d’identité, un justificatif de résidence et un dépôt initial dont le montant dépend du type de compte choisi. Pour les entreprises, des documents complémentaires relatifs à la société sont nécessaires, en fonction notamment de sa forme juridique. La responsable de Coris Bank Internationale Guinée a également insisté sur un point qu’elle considère comme essentiel : la finance islamique n’est pas une finance confessionnelle. « Il ne faut pas confondre la finance islamique en pensant que c’est un truc qui est destiné seulement aux musulmans. La finance islamique, Baraka est là pour tout le monde », a-t-elle affirmé. Présent à cette rencontre, Dr Mamadou Tafsir Baldé, représentant de SONOCO WAQF, s’est pour sa part réjoui de la richesse des échanges. Il a salué l’expertise et l’expérience partagées par l’expert en finance islamique ainsi que les réponses apportées aux préoccupations des participants. Pour lui, cette rencontre constitue une source supplémentaire de motivation pour les acteurs intéressés par le développement de la finance islamique en Guinée. Il a encouragé les personnes qui hésitent encore à s’engager dans ce secteur à s’intéresser davantage aux solutions proposées par Coris Bank Baraka. A travers cette rencontre organisée à Kipé, Coris Bank Internationale Guinée entend ainsi contribuer à une meilleure compréhension de la finance islamique et de ses mécanismes. Entre financement des entreprises, accompagnement des PME, solutions pour les particuliers et exigence de conformité, les différents intervenants ont défendu une vision d’une finance à la fois éthique, accessible et tournée vers les besoins de l’économie guinéenne. Le message porté au cours de cette rencontre est donc sans ambiguïté : la finance islamique ne se limite pas à une appartenance religieuse. Elle se veut avant tout une finance fondée sur des principes éthiques, ouverte à tous et capable d’accompagner durablement les particuliers, les entreprises et les PME en Guinée.

items.title: Navy, Army, Police rescue 13 kidnap victims in Kogi, arrest six drug suspects in Rivers
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — The Nigerian Navy, in collaboration with the Nigerian Army, Nigeria Police Force and local vigilantes, has rescued 13 kidnapped victims in Kogi State and arrested six suspected drug peddlers in Rivers State. The Director of Information, Nigerian Navy, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday. He said the 13 victims were rescued along the Itobe–Anyigba Highway in Ofu Local Government Area of Kogi State on August 10, following a reported kidnapping incident. According to him, the operation involved a coordinated search and rescue effort by personnel of the Navy, Army, Police and local vigilantes. “The victims were subsequently placed under the care of relevant security authorities for screening and necessary assistance,” he said. Folorunsho said the joint team encountered resistance from suspected kidnappers during the operation. He disclosed that one vigilante personnel was killed, while a police officer sustained a gunshot injury and was evacuated for medical attention. He added that security operations had been intensified in the area as efforts continued to locate and arrest the fleeing suspects. In Rivers State, the Navy said personnel of Forward Operating Base Bonny, in collaboration with the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), Bonny Area Command, arrested six suspected drug peddlers during an intelligence-driven operation at Amahausa, Bonny Local Government Area. The operation also led to the recovery of various illicit substances, including 250 tablets of Exol 5, 117 wraps of Cannabis Sativa, 50 wraps of methamphetamine, 70 wraps of heroin, eight capsules of 100mg Tramadol, three packs of Cannabis Sativa and a methamphetamine pipe. The Navy said the operations demonstrated the impact of intelligence-led action, rapid response and inter-agency cooperation in tackling criminal activities. It added that the operations were part of efforts to deny criminal elements freedom of action, protect lives and support broader national efforts to strengthen security across communities and Nigeria’s maritime environment. items.title: Sekyedumase Community Bank sues Asokore Mampong Assembly over demolition for 24-hour economy market
items.description: A legal dispute is brewing between the Sekyedumase Community Bank and the Asokore Mampong Municipal Assembly in the Ashanti Region following an alleged unlawful demolition of the bank’s building for the construction of a 24-hour economy market. The bank’s management claims the Assembly acted unlawfully by demolishing the facility while applications concerning the property were still pending before the courts in Kumasi. The bank, which has operated in the Aboabo community for decades, is now conducting its operations from a makeshift stall after its building was pulled down along with other shops and homes in the area. The demolition was carried out on Monday by a security taskforce from the Asokore Mampong Assembly as part of preparations for the municipality’s 24-hour economy market project. Management of the bank says it had engaged the Assembly for several months over the proposed redevelopment of the area and possible relocation or integration of the bank into the project. However, the bank says its concerns were not addressed, forcing it to seek legal redress over the land it claims ownership of. Counsel for the Sekyedumase Community Bank, Dr Dickson Osei Assibey, said the bank had occupied the land for more than three decades and had constructed the building with its own resources. He said the bank was prepared to engage the Assembly but believed its proposal to integrate the existing facility into the 24-hour economy project was not given fair consideration. “The bank has been there over 33 years. And from the documents that are on the land, it shows that the community gave the land to the bank to develop it as a bank to serve them. So the bank put up the building by themselves. It’s not the community. It’s not the municipal assembly. It is for the bank. And then the bank has been there for the past 33 years.” Dr Assibey said the bank had been willing to explore an amicable solution, including having its facility incorporated into the new market development. “So even if you want them to move, it’s a matter of talking with each other, which they started. But the position of the bank was that either you integrate our building into the 24-hour economy project, which to me it is possible. They have not been fair. They have trespassed, and we think that the court have to take that matter up.” Chief Executive Officer of the bank, Afriyie Michael Kwabena, said the demolition had resulted in the destruction of physical assets worth millions of Ghanaian cedis. He said while the bank’s customer database had been preserved through its digital systems, equipment and other physical assets inside the building were lost. “We have inventory of all the assets that is in the building. And the customer database is intact because due to technology and the existence of the bank for the past 46 years, we have managed to have the data of the customers intact. So for customer data, it’s not lost. But the physical items of the bank are lost, running into millions of Ghanaian cedis.” Mr Afriyie also disputed claims that the bank had been formally evicted before the demolition. “We are not served any eviction notice. In fact, we have for the past five months been cooperating with the Assembly. We have not been served any eviction notice.” The Asokore Mampong Municipal Assembly is yet to comment on the allegations by the bank. In the meantime, management says it is working with ARB Apex Bank and the Bank of Ghana to secure an alternative location from which the bank can continue its operations. The legal dispute is expected to continue in court, with the two applications filed by the opposing sides expected to be heard in October.

items.title: Solar eclipse sweeps across UK, parts of Europe
items.description: A rare solar eclipse is underway across the United Kingdom and parts of Europe, as the Moon moves between the Earth and the Sun, temporarily blocking part of the Sun’s light. The eclipse became visible in Edinburgh at about 6:28pm BST on Wednesday, with the phenomenon expected to reach its peak in the Scottish capital at around 7:06pm. According to the BBC, observers at Calton Hill in Edinburgh watched as the Moon gradually moved across the Sun, with sunspots reportedly visible through a telescope. The eclipse had already begun in parts of Iceland and Greenland, while several other European countries were expected to experience a total eclipse as the Moon moved along its path. More than 90 per cent of the Sun was expected to be obscured across much of the UK, making the event the most significant solar eclipse visible from the country since 1999. The spectacle attracted large crowds to viewing sites across the UK, with reports that specialist eclipse glasses had sold out in some locations. Russia, Spain witness eclipse The eclipse first reached the northernmost part of mainland Russia at about 1700 GMT, where the Moon covered the Sun and left the outer corona visible against the darkened sky. The eclipse then moved across Greenland and Iceland before reaching Spain, where its path stretched diagonally from the northwestern Atlantic coast towards the Mediterranean. Large numbers of tourists and astronomy enthusiasts gathered in Spanish towns and villages to witness the event, amid heightened interest because mainland Europe had not experienced a total solar eclipse for two decades. Spain, in particular, had not witnessed a total solar eclipse for more than 100 years. A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes directly between the Earth and the Sun, casting its shadow on Earth and blocking some or all of the Sun from view. Experts have warned observers against looking directly at the Sun without certified eye protection, as doing so can cause serious and permanent damage to the eyes. The eclipse has also attracted scientific interest, with Irish researchers planning to travel across the Atlantic to study the Sun’s outer atmosphere, known as the corona, during the event. items.title: “I’m partially single” – Tima Kumkum finally breaks silence on divorce rumours
items.description: Media personality Cynthia Tima Yeboah, popularly known as Tima Kumkum, has confirmed that she is separated from her husband, Dominic Duodu, and that their divorce is currently before the court. Speaking to Nikki Samonas on Joy Prime’s Changes show, Tima Kumkum said the couple have not lived together since 1 April 2025 and that she considers herself ‘partially single’ because she is not yet divorced. “I said I was not going to talk about it. People have been forcing me to say it. I’m separated. Not yet divorced but will be divorced soon. I didn’t want to talk about it but let’s call a spade a spade; we don’t live together since 1st April, 2025. So, I’m partially single because I’m not fully divorced yet but it’s in court so we don’t really want to talk about it,” she revealed. The media personality had previously been at the centre of speculation after she was seen without her wedding ring for several months, prompting some social media users to suggest that she had divorced her husband. Tima later addressed the rumours in a post on her social media platforms, debunking the claims and explaining why she had stopped wearing her wedding ring. During the interview, the question about the whereabouts of her ‘supposed’ current husband came up after Tima revealed that she had been solely responsible for taking care of her children without support from any man. She added that people in the area where she lives are aware of the situation, so it is not news to them. However, she is not willing to disclose the reason for the breakup, even after the divorce process is successfully completed in court. Tima Kumkum said she never thought such an incident would happen again, especially since it was her second marriage. However, the couple lived together for one year and nine months before eventually separating. She also commended her ex-husband, Dominic Duodu, for being a responsible father and taking care of their child since their separation. “He’s a very responsible man. I’ll give him his flowers for that. He takes care of his child and pays his school fees. That’s fine and I’m okay with that. So, custody is okay,” Tima further said. For now, she said she has no plans to marry again, adding that marriage is currently the last thing on her mind.

items.title: Dangote Cement, Ibese, FRSC strengthen partnership to advance road safety in Ogun
items.description: By Faith Odukomaiya Efforts aimed at further enhancing road safety in Ogun State has received a boost following fresh collaborative engagement between the Dangote Cement Plc, Ibese Plant and the State Sector Command for safer road use and general safety advocacy. Dangote Cement Plc, Ibese Plant reaffirmed its commitment to promoting safer roads and strengthening stakeholder collaboration as it received the newly deployed Ogun State Sector Commander of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Corps Commander Oludare Ogunjobi, and members of his management team on a courtesy visit to the plant. The visit provided an opportunity for both organizations to discuss strategies for enhancing road safety awareness, driver competence, and regulatory compliance across Ogun State. Speaking during the engagement, Corps Commander Ogunjobi commended Dangote Cement for its consistent support to the FRSC and its contribution to road safety initiatives over the years pointing out that the company has established itself as one of the Corps’ most reliable corporate partners through its commitment to safety and responsible transportation practices. Said he; “Dangote Cement has remained a dependable partner of the Federal Road Safety Corps over the years, and we deeply appreciate the support we have continued to receive from the company,” Ogunjobi said. “As an organization with extensive logistics and transportation operations, Dangote Cement understands the importance of safety on our roads. This shared commitment provides a strong foundation for even greater collaboration between our two institutions.” The Sector Commander emphasized that promoting a culture of safety requires continuous engagement with stakeholders, particularly organizations that operate large fleets of vehicles and professional drivers. “Road safety is not the responsibility of FRSC alone. It requires collective action from government agencies, private sector organizations, transport operators, and road users. We believe there is significant potential for us to work more closely with Dangote Cement in driving safety awareness and improving compliance with road traffic regulations,” he stated. As part of the proposed areas of cooperation, Ogunjobi advocated the establishment of an FRSC Special Marshal Unit within the Ibese Plant, noting that the initiative would strengthen safety consciousness among employees and drivers. “We would like to see the establishment of an in-plant FRSC Special Marshal Unit that will serve as a platform for promoting road safety advocacy and best practices among staff and transport operators. Such a unit will support specialized driver training programmes, regular sensitization sessions, and proactive safety campaigns aimed at reducing road crashes, he said. He further assured the company of the Corps’ readiness to provide technical support saying “our doors remain open. We are committed to supporting Dangote Cement through continuous engagement, capacity building and safety enlightenment initiatives that will ultimately benefit not just the company but all road users across Ogun State,” he added. Responding, the Plant Director of Dangote Cement Plc, Ibese Plant, Mr. Ayyagri Subbaraidu, described the FRSC as a critical stakeholder in the company’s operations and commended the Corps for its dedication to preserving lives on Nigerian roads. While noting that safety remains a central pillar of Dangote Cement’s operational philosophy and long-term growth strategy. “The Federal Road Safety Corps plays a strategic role in our operations because transportation is a vital component of our business. We therefore recognize and appreciate the tremendous work being done by the Corps in ensuring safer roads and protecting lives,” Subbaraidu said. The Plant Director explained that the company’s Vision 2030 places strong emphasis on responsible operations, sustainability, and stakeholder collaboration, making road safety an important priority. “Dangote Vision 2030 clearly highlights the need for stronger partnerships with key stakeholders such as the FRSC. Safety is not merely a regulatory requirement for us; it is a core value that guides how we operate every day,” he stated. “Our commitment goes beyond the movement of products. We are committed to ensuring that our drivers, contractors, employees and every road user interacting with our operations do so in the safest possible environment.” Subbaraidu welcomed the proposals presented by the new Sector Commander and assured the visiting delegation that Management would continue to explore initiatives capable of strengthening the existing relationship. “We appreciate the suggestions put forward by the Sector Commander, particularly in the area of driver education and safety awareness. These initiatives align with our commitment to continuous improvement in health, safety and operational excellence,” he said. “Dangote Cement remains ready to work hand in hand with the FRSC in advancing road safety campaigns, improving driver competence, enhancing compliance, and creating safer roads for all. We look forward to expanding our collaboration for the mutual benefit of our organizations and the communities we serve.” The visit ended with both parties expressing confidence that a stronger partnership between Dangote Cement and the FRSC would significantly contribute to safer road transportation, improved driver behaviour, and enhanced compliance with safety regulations across Ogun State. The post Dangote Cement, Ibese, FRSC strengthen partnership to advance road safety in Ogun appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Govt cuts petrol price by Re0.94, raises high-speed diesel by Re0.54
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Wednesday reduced the price of petrol by Re0.94 and increased the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.54 per litre. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs324.98 per litre while HSD will cost Rs382.79 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on HSD. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable for August 13 (Thursday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: American Cola launches Ilupeju Creative Court with sports contests
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab American Cola has unveiled its newly renovated basketball court in Ilupeju, Lagos, as part of its efforts to support grassroots basketball and provide better facilities for young talents in the community. The unveiling, held in partnership with the Odi-Olowo/Ojuwoye Local Council Development Area, also featured the presentation of new jerseys to the council’s male and female basketball teams, as well as the second edition of the American Cola Shoot the Hoop and Half Court tournaments. The revamped facility, now known as the American Cola Creative Court, is expected to serve as a platform for basketball development while providing young people with opportunities to engage in other creative and cultural activities. Marketing Manager of Planet Bottling Company, Naji Awada, while speaking during the unveiling, said the initiative was designed to go beyond the physical renovation of the court and help nurture talents. “This project is not about paint, new hoops, or putting up a logo on that fence. It’s about renewing the passion for basketball, bringing talent into this court, hopefully seeing stars because of this court. “And it’s about bringing communities together, building friendships, building memories, and hopefully building a future for one of these great talents that we have here today.” Awada said the company was looking beyond the Ilupeju project, noting that it intended to replicate similar initiatives in other communities. “Hopefully it will not be the last project when it comes to basketball. We are looking to do more, especially in different communities, to bring together all of the people under the same roof, which is the talent that mostly we miss out on, because no one is giving them the right attention. “Hopefully we will be on that road, and we will do such beautiful things for that sport.” Also speaking, Communications Manager of Planet Bottling Company, Franklyn Eluagu, said the company was identifying basketball communities across Lagos where it could improve playing facilities and create better conditions for players. “For American Cola globally, the countries that we belong to, we love basketball. And all the communities that play basketball in Lagos, starting with Lagos, we are identifying them and seeing what we can do as a brand to improve the conditions when it comes to the community and the courts for the basketball players.” Eluagu said the initiative was aimed at contributing to the growth of basketball in Lagos and other parts of the country. “For the youth, this would bring a place for them to, beyond basketball, hone their skills. So for those who love graffiti, for those who love music, for those who love dance, it’s made the court to look a lot better in terms of the beauty of the court.” He added that the facility would provide an avenue for young people and schools interested in basketball to develop and showcase their talents. “For the communities, schools that love basketball can find a place that they can come to and feel very welcome in terms of what their skills are and the talent that they’re trying to showcase.” Meanwhile, Chairman of the Odi-Olowo/Ojuwoye Local Council Development Area, Oduwoye, said the project had already begun attracting residents from the community and neighbouring local governments. “It has already started benefiting the people of Ilupeju. As you can see, we have a lot of fans here today. And it’s not only from Odi-Olowo, we have people from other local governments also coming to use this pitch.” He described the facility as an outdoor standard sporting space with fitness facilities, adding that the partnership had brought renewed activity to the community. “For us, it’s a bit of pride for the local government that American Cola partnered with us and is a beneficiary partner with us, and has also brought more life to our local government.” Oduwoye said the project also aligned with the council’s efforts to engage young people through sports and provide alternatives to street activities. “It’s not only about American Cola, it’s also about the local government showing special support and taking steps to take the youth out of the streets.” He further disclosed that discussions were underway to extend the partnership beyond basketball to other sports and recreational facilities within the council area. According to him, the council has identified about five parks in Odi-Olowo and Ilupeju that could benefit from similar interventions. “In Odi-Olowo or Ilupeju Estate, we have about five parks which I’ve highlighted to the managing director. These parks are there, they’re parks but they’re not as active as before.” Oduwoye said the council would continue discussions with American Cola on how the facilities could be revitalised and made more useful to residents. “We have plans to extend this beyond basketball with American Cola, and then want to do things like football or maybe other sports.” The unveiling coincided with the second edition of the American Cola Shoot the Hoop and Half Court tournaments, which featured 24 teams in each competition. Some of the matches were played during the unveiling, with participating teams competing for a combined ₦5m prize pool. The winner of the Shoot the Hoop competition will receive ₦800,000, while the second- and third-placed teams will receive ₦400,000 and ₦200,000, respectively. For the Half Court competition, the winners will receive ₦2m, while the runners-up and third-placed team will get ₦1m and ₦500,000, respectively. The unveiling forms part of American Cola’s broader community and grassroots sports initiative, with the company signalling plans to take similar projects to other communities. items.title: I’ve been the only one taking care of my kids for 14 years; no man has helped me – Tima Kumkum
items.description: Media personality Cynthia Tima Yeboah, widely known as Tima Kumkum, has revealed that she has been the sole caretaker of all her children for the past 14 years. The revelation came while she was reminiscing about the difficult periods in her career and marriage on Joy Prime’s Changes show. During the interview with Nikki Samonas, Tima Kumkum stated that she struggled to care for her second child alone after divorcing her husband, while she was also still building her career. “For 14 years, I’ve been the one paying their school fees, taking care of them, shelter, clothes and everything. So if I’ve not been able to even finish building my house, it’s because of my kids,” she said. Asked where her ex-husband was at the time and why she had to juggle everything by herself, the Adom TV presenter replied, “He was around the world. I always say it anyway, not because I’m disgracing him. I’ll never do that because he’s the father of my kids, but he hasn’t been involved with my kids.” According to her, her first child has completed JHS and is about to continue to SHS, while her second child is currently in JHS 2 and will be moving on to SHS in two years. She said all their expenses have been solely her responsibility. As a mother of three, Tima Kumkum said she never gave up on herself or her children. Instead, she remained strong and persevered for the sake of her kids. Reflecting on the difficulties she has faced in her career and marriage, Tima Kumkum is set to host an all-women conference, “Be Inspired by Tima Women’s Conference 2026”, themed “Turning Pain into Purpose”. The conference seeks to inspire and support young women facing similar emotional, mental and physical challenges. The event will feature speakers with lived experiences, including suicide prevention advocate Gloria Boatemaa Andoh, entrepreneur Maame Joe, and burns survivor and globally recognised advocate Judith Cato Addison, alongside an engaging panel discussion. The event is scheduled for Saturday, 12 September 2026, at Villa Vista, East Legon, ahead of Tima’s birthday celebration on 17 September. Other notable personalities expected to be involved include General Overseer of Faithway International Chapel, Pastor Selina; Mrs Mary Amoah Kuffour, Founder of Klicks Foundation; and Mrs Naa Joe Bechem, CEO of RJ’s Events & More and Proprietor of The Beechams Montessori. The “Be Inspired by Tima Women’s Conference” promises honest conversations and practical life lessons from women who have turned adversity into purpose.
